notes: Category 3 of the taxonomy in docs/pool_edge_plan.md: the interval contains both zero AND the hypothesised effect, so the test said nothing. These are NOT negatives.
The evaluator resolves ~2 ATS points (RWB-15). Most single features are worth a fraction of that, so landing here is the DEFAULT outcome for a real small signal.
Effects are stored so POSITIVE FAVOURS THE CANDIDATE regardless of the metric's own polarity; Brier and MAE must be negated before recording.
A pooled estimate justifies ONE predeclared combined look on a rotation window none of the inputs touched. It is never itself a finding.

bye_overval_fade_stacked_on_production.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% CI [-0.4670, +1.6880] accuracy points, P+ 0.8474 (n=1503 games, 107 week-blocks); season-blocked secondary 95% CI [+0.1266, +1.4175], P+ 0.9980 (6 season-blocks). Point estimate is POSITIVE on both blockings; the week-blocked interval crosses zero and the season-blocked interval sits entirely ABOVE zero, so wrong_sign_resolved (which requires the WHOLE interval below zero on BOTH blockings) does not apply; no positive control was run against this stacked form, so positive_control_bound does not apply either. Per AGENTS.md an interval crossing zero is never grounds to close a line of work -- this is a mined-seasons read (already-looked-at 2020-2025 opener archive) offered as CONTEXT for the registration decision, not a gate; the underlying registry cell bye_overval_fade_full_slate_post2011 (week-blocked P+ 0.8375, n=2171, seasons 2012-2025) is the primary evidence.
bye_overval_fade_stacked_on_production.description: bye_edge_fade_overlay (fade the strict, >=12-day-gap bye-holding side wherever exactly one team is off a strict bye and the model's own pick sits on that side) stacked on top of the active model's own opener-graded PRODUCTION picks, REG 2020-2025, 1503 scored games, 68 games flipped.
bye_overval_fade_stacked_on_production.notes: Stacked-on-production read for the bye_edge_fade_overlay prospective challenger (scripts/bye_edge_fade_stacked_backtest.py; docs/bye_edge_fade_overlay.md). n_flipped=68 of 1537 games. Baseline is the active model's own opener-graded production card (artifacts/opener_evaluation/20260819T174244Z/per_game.parquet), not a synthetic baseline.
bye_overval_fade_stacked_on_production.plain_summary: Teams coming off a real bye often get overrated by the market; this fades them, flipping the pick away from the rested team whenever the model's own pick was already on that side. Layered on top of what the model actually plays across 1,503 graded games (2020-2025), it flips 68 games and nudges accuracy from 53.36% to about 53.96% -- a small move that is mostly favorable: the week-by-week read still crosses zero, but the season-by-season read is fully positive.

bye_overval_install_need_moderator.description: Difference-in-differences inside the post-2011-CBA bye population (REG 2012-2025, non-push home_cover): the bye-overvaluation home-edge effect for install-need home teams minus the same effect for continuity home teams. Base flag imported verbatim from scripts/bye_overvaluation_screen.py (home off strict >=12-day bye AND opponent not off bye). Moderator = the home team season-opener starting QB differs from the prior season opener starting QB. Predeclared one-sided direction: contrast > 0.
bye_overval_install_need_moderator.notes: Predeclared in docs/era_mechanism_screens_20260901.md section 2.1 BEFORE any effect was computed; proposed unrun in docs/era_magnitude_report.md section 2.1. Season-blocked secondary +0.1855 [-1.0284, +1.3405] P+=0.6298 on 14 blocks. Within-week permutation null (200 draws, NOT zero-centred by design): null mean +0.1235, [-0.7002, +1.0221]; 44 percent of null draws sit at or above the observed +0.1855. Arm magnitudes: install-need -0.2289, no-need -0.4143 (post-2011); pre-2011 control arms -0.3404 and +0.8915 on 35 flagged games - four magnitudes, never averaged across the parent construct era sign flip. DISCLOSED: the predeclared moderator was new QB OR new offensive coordinator; no offensive-coordinator source exists in this repo (measured), so only the QB leg is built - a strictly NARROWER subset that dilutes the contrast toward zero. DISCLOSED OVERLAP: same rows as bye_overval_home_edge_post2011 and a subset of venue_milestone_post_bye_home; correlated, never an independent vote, never sign-test-pooled with them. Mined-window discount: runs on the full history including the mined 2018-2025 seasons. n_flag 87 install-need / 151 no-need. Battery multiplicity uncorrected (3 cells + 1 companion arm).
bye_overval_install_need_moderator.plain_summary: Teams coming off a bye have gotten a bit worse against the spread since the 2011 labour deal cut practice time. This checks whether that penalty is smaller for teams with a new starting quarterback, who have more to install and more to gain from the extra week. It leans that way, but nowhere near enough to act on.

cfb_altitude_cold_home_on_benchmark.description: CFB altitude-plus-cold home (LEAD-46): backs the home team at a frozen list of Mountain-West altitude venues from October onward, on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm
cfb_altitude_cold_home_on_benchmark.notes: Unsigned flag (1 iff home_team in {Colorado State, Wyoming, Air Force, Utah} AND gameday.month>=10; else 0) on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm. No local elevation/venue table exists (measured: data/cfb/team_info carries only venue_name/city/state, no elevation figure), so the frozen ROADMAP-named Mountain-West altitude list stands in. No local weather/temperature column exists either, so 'cold' is calendar-proxied (October on), not a verified temperature reading -- disclosed, not assumed. 191 flagged of 8933 clean-core games (thin by construction, 4 programs' Oct-on home slates), 0 missing. Positive control +48.405 pts P+ 1.000. Per-era: 2012-2019 +0.075 pts P+ 0.657; 2021-2025 -0.335 pts P+ 0.086 (CI [-0.806,+0.144] still contains zero). New family, distinct from cfb_rest_bye_replication/cfb_option_prep_screen. Close-graded CFB; no NFL window spent.
cfb_altitude_cold_home_on_benchmark.plain_summary: Backing the four Mountain-West altitude home teams late in the season leans slightly against the idea pooled across 2012-2025, but the sample is thin and the two eras disagree.

The week-blocked 95% interval [-0.1208, +0.1013] crosses zero at this evaluator's resolution -- the EXPECTED shape for a real-but-small signal, never grounds to close per AGENTS.md. cfb_body_clock_east_host_west_visitor_ea.description: CFB replication of NFL body_clock_east_host_west_visitor_early: Eastern-clock host receiving a Pacific/Arizona-body-clock visitor, kickoff before 14:00 ET, neutral sites excluded as NaN. Eastern host is tested on the venue UTC offset at kickoff rather than a literal America/New_York string, which keeps the Michigan and Indiana hosts a string test would drop (8 of the 24 flagged games).
cfb_body_clock_east_host_west_visitor_ea.notes: CLOSE-GRADED CFB: the CFB archive carries no verified opener (docs/cfb_data.md:42), so this is graded on the median-book close-proxy spread_line. A CFB result is replication evidence about a mechanism and never by itself changes an NFL card. No NFL evaluation window and no rotation window was spent. The four cells in family cfb_body_clock_replication are CORRELATED SUBSETS of one window and are NOT independent votes: east_host_west_visitor_early is a strict subset of west_road_early (24 of its 50 flagged games), night_west_road shares the identical body-clock definition at the opposite end of the kickoff distribution, and eastbound_multizone overlaps all three through the same timezone map. Never sign-test-pool them, and never pool them with the NFL siblings (different league, different grade, different baseline). Registered effect is the PRIMARY estimator: paired candidate-minus-baseline forced-pick accuracy delta, frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm (35 columns, ridge alpha 10, market-residual target, 500-game training floor, weekly refits trained strictly before each scored week) versus the identical estimator plus exactly this one column. Scored population 8,933 games / 199 week blocks / 13 seasons, with 271 neutral-site rows carrying NaN. Replicates NFL sibling body_clock_east_host_west_visitor_early (registry effect -0.2690, 95% [-0.6232, +0.0917], P+ 0.0714). Season-blocked secondary: 95% [-0.1340, +0.1141], P+ 0.381. SECONDARY NFL-COMMENSURABLE estimator (subset-vs-complement full-slate-scaled home_cover gap, scripts/_common.summarize, 20,000 draws): +0.0017 pts, week 95% [-0.0524, +0.0551], P+ 0.5348, season P+ 0.5382, n_flag 24, subset cover 50.00% vs complement 49.37%, raw gap +0.634 pts -- the OPPOSITE side of zero from the NFL sibling, so the NFL direction did not replicate. Per-era primary magnitudes carry OPPOSITE SIGNS (2012-2019 +0.0561, P+ 0.738; 2021-2025 -0.1116, P+ 0.034), so this pooled number is an average across a sign flip and must not be read as either era's magnitude -- both era slices are recorded separately as cfb_body_clock_east_host_west_visitor_early_era_2012_2019 and _era_2021_2025. Headroom note: 24 flagged games are 0.27% of the scored slate. Instrument checks: within-week permutation null (200 draws) mean +0.021/-0.004/+0.030/+0.007 pts across the four cells, all centred within 0.03 points of zero; positive control (candidate column replaced by realised ats_margin) +48.405 accuracy points, P+ 1.000, 95% [+47.374, +49.464] on n=8,933 -- so the full 36-column ridge fit is not blind to a real effect of meaningful size. RELIABILITY FIELD carries the underlying body-clock UTC-offset trait: Pearson r 0.9858 95% [0.9843, 0.9871], Spearman-Brown 0.9928, n=2,420 team-seasons (odd/even-week split-half). The per-cell EXPOSURE propensities are, for the record: west_road_early SB 0.0990 (r 0.0521, 95% [-0.0121, +0.1966], P+ 0.6245); east_host_west_visitor_early SB -0.0075 (r -0.0037, 95% [-0.0060, -0.0019], P+ 0.0000); eastbound_multizone SB 0.5608 (r 0.3897, P+ 1.0000); night_west_road SB 0.7434 (r 0.5916, P+ 1.0000). For a per-team-season event that happens at most once, a positive in the odd half nearly always implies a zero in the even half, which forces a small negative odd/even correlation by construction, so the two thin cells' exposure figures measure RARITY, not the reliability of a trait. The AGENTS.md rationale for the no_split_half_reliability ground (no sample size rescues it) is false for a rare schedule fact, so that ground is NOT admissible for any cell in this family. cfb_portal_qb_early_on_benchmark.description: CFB portal-QB early starts (LEAD-49): signed column fading a team starting an early-tenure (first three games) transfer-portal QB, on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm
cfb_portal_qb_early_on_benchmark.notes: Signed column cfb_lead49_portal_qb_early_signed: +1 when the AWAY team's pregame-safe presumed starter (leading passer of that team's most recently completed EARLIER game, point-in-time lookup) is one of that team's matched transfer-portal QB arrivals this season AND this is within that team's first three games of the season, -1 mirror, 0 otherwise/both. Population restricted to 2021-2025 (CFBD portal data starts 2021; single era, no split). Portal identity match (name+school+season, disclosed per CFBD_PORTAL_IDENTITY_CONTRACT): 807 portal QB rows, 39 unresolved destinations, 35 ambiguous roster-name keys excluded (never guessed), 658 matched (81.5%), covering 490 distinct team-seasons. Starter-agreement diagnostic (previous known starter vs. same game's own post-hoc starter, general QB continuity, not portal-specific): 81.7% (6772 comparable games). 163 flagged of 3584 scored games / 77 weeks (95 away-side, 106 home-side, 19 games where both sides independently qualified and cancel to 0 per the signed convention). STRUCTURAL DISCLOSURE: because a portal transfer cannot have started an earlier game for their new team, the pregame-safe flag can never fire on a team's first game of the season for its incoming portal QB -- only games 2-3 of the nominal 'first three'; the coverage numbers above reflect that narrower, leak-safe population, not the full three-game window. Positive control +48.493 pts P+ 1.000. Week-blocked P+ 0.098, season-blocked P+ 0.11 -- leans strongly AGAINST the predicted FADE direction (i.e. holding the market side beats fading it here) but the week-blocked interval [-0.00687,+0.00188] pts still contains a positive tail, so this is NOT wrong_sign_resolved (the whole interval must sit below zero); stays unresolved_below_power. Null observed at the 4th percentile (mean +0.107 pts). Never pooled with XLG-06's recruiting-rating entries (no recruiting rating or star count is read anywhere in this construct, only portal transfer records and play-by-play passer identity). Close-graded CFB; no NFL window spent or earned.

cfb_qb_dependence_interaction.classification_evidence: Week-blocked accuracy P+=0.5140 (below 0.75 clear bar), Brier P+=0.3633 with no resolved gain (below 0.90 bar); both 95% intervals straddle zero comfortably (do not exclude zero on the wrong side, so bounded_by_control does not apply). Point estimate (+0.0224 pts) sits at ~2.05% of this screen's own MDE80 floor (1.093 pts, f=0.1385, n=9093) -- below detection power, not evidence of zero effect. Step 0 split-half reliability is 0.9588 (interaction), 0.9581/0.9923 (constituents) -- far above this repo's no-split-half-reliability examples (0.063, 0.014) and even above its own cleared precedents (0.68-0.93), ruling out refuted_mechanism.
cfb_qb_dependence_interaction.description: CFB QB-dependence interaction (raw qb_starter_epa_per_dropback x off_pass_rate, per side, differenced) vs the frozen XLG-03 CFB benchmark, candidate adds the interaction plus its two constituent diff columns alongside the baseline.

cfb_rest_away_off_bye_on_benchmark.classification_evidence: Predeclared cell frozen before scoring in docs/cfb_rest_bye_replication.md (sections 1-8 written and saved before any scoring mode ran; section 5 filled from a PREDICTOR-ONLY coverage run). Neither admissible closing ground applies: wrong_sign_resolved requires the WHOLE week-blocked interval on the wrong side of zero and this one is [-0.3754, +0.6059]; positive_control_bound requires the instrument to have been PROVEN able to detect an effect of THIS size, and the control only proved detection of a +48.4-point leak; no_split_half_reliability is unavailable both because the correctly-specified across-season split-half reads Spearman-Brown 0.8271 (far above the 0.10 ceiling the ground admits) and because a deterministic calendar fact has zero measurement error. cfb_rest_away_off_bye_on_benchmark.description: CFB replication of NFL travel_rest_away_off_bye: away_rest >= 13 days (side-specific absolute threshold, away mirror) added as ONE extra column to the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm, which already carries rest_diff. Paired candidate-minus-baseline forced-pick accuracy delta; positive = the extra column helped. NFL predicted direction on home_cover: negative.
cfb_rest_away_off_bye_on_benchmark.notes: POOLED read over the frozen clean core 2012-2019 + 2021-2025 (8933 games, 199 week blocks, 13 seasons, 1001 flagged, 523 feature-missing season-opener rows). Season-blocked secondary: 95% [-0.3333, +0.5255] P+ 0.6760. Observed delta sits at the 60.5th percentile of its own within-week permutation null. PER-ERA MAGNITUDES (owner rule 'era magnitude, not presence' -- never average across a sign flip): 2012-2019 +0.093 pts P+ 0.645 95% [-0.508, +0.665] n=5349 flagged=605; 2021-2025 +0.112 pts P+ 0.588 95% [-0.731, +0.906] n=3584 flagged=396. Close-graded CFB: the CFB line archive is opener plus an unidentified-time resolved quote and no source records quote observation times (docs/cfb_data.md), so CFB can be graded at a close proxy and NEVER at a verified opener; this settles no NFL play/no-play or promotion decision. THE BASELINE ALREADY CARRIES rest_diff: nfl_ats.cfb_features.CFB_MODEL_FEATURE_COLUMNS (35 columns) includes rest_diff, so this is a MARGINAL on top of a model that already prices the linear rest difference, not a test of whether rest matters. NFL sibling entry: travel_rest_away_off_bye. The four cells of this battery are CORRELATED SUBSETS OF ONE WINDOW (the same 8,933 scored games, overlapping flags by construction) and are NOT independent votes -- do not sign-test-pool them. OVERLAP DISCLOSURE: separate pooling family cfb_rest_bye_replication, NEVER pooled with cfb_bias_battery. registry entries cfb_bias_battery_bye_week_rest_edge (rest edge >=6d) and cfb_bias_battery_short_week_rest_disadvantage (rest edge <=-4d) are SUBSET COVER RATE VS COMPLEMENT measurements on an overlapping CFB population -- a different quantity from this harness's paired accuracy delta of the XLG-03 estimator with exactly one extra column; AGENTS.md's commensurability rule forbids pooling non-commensurable comparators. The repo-standard WITHIN-season odd/even-WEEK instrument reads r -0.3368 on the same panel; that is a structural artifact of a compositionally constrained calendar quantity (a team-season holds a fixed number of days and games, so extra rest in one part is arithmetically less rest elsewhere), not evidence about the trait -- docs/cfb_rest_bye_replication.md section 5. Seed 20260901, 1,000 bootstrap draws. Within-week permutation null (200 draws, standalone run artifacts/cfb_rest_bye_replication/20260901T193006Z): mean +0.044 pts, sd 0.233, 95% [-0.403, +0.505] -- the harness manufactures no effect. Positive control (this column replaced by the realised ats_margin, artifacts/cfb_rest_bye_replication/20260901T193332Z): +48.405 pts, P+ 1.000, 95% [+47.374, +49.464] -- the full 36-column ridge fit detects a large effect, which bounds NOTHING at the sub-1-point scale in question. XLG-03 baseline forced-pick accuracy on this population: 51.595%.

cfb_rivalry_home_dog_on_benchmark.description: CFB rivalry home dog (LEAD-50): backs the home underdog in a deterministically-identified rivalry-pair game, on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm
cfb_rivalry_home_dog_on_benchmark.notes: Unsigned flag (1 iff a rivalry-pair game AND home is the market underdog, spread_line<0; else 0) on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm. No local rivalry field exists on the CFBD schedule rows (measured: only 3 of 36915 rows mention 'rival' in free-text notes, all one bowl name); rivalry pairs are the deterministic proxy declared in this lane's task -- same team pair met in >=8 consecutive seasons anywhere in the full local schedule history (521 pairs qualify). Disclosed limitation: this captures true historic rivalries (Army-Navy, Auburn-Alabama) but also long-running conference-mandated annual pairings -- no local field disambiguates the two. 4459 rivalry-pair games, 3439 home-underdog games, 1852 flagged (both) of 8933 clean-core games, 0 missing. Positive control +48.405 pts P+ 1.000. Per-era: 2012-2019 +0.037 pts P+ 0.547; 2021-2025 -0.028 pts P+ 0.429 -- both noise-scale (<0.04 pts, P+ within 0.06 of a coin flip), not recorded as separate rows. New family, distinct from the deployed NFL division-revenge overlay and from cfb_rest_bye_replication/cfb_option_prep_screen. Close-graded CFB; no NFL window spent.
cfb_rivalry_home_dog_on_benchmark.plain_summary: Backing the home underdog in a long-running CFB rivalry game is basically a coin flip, tilted very slightly toward working.

cfb_role_continuity.classification_evidence: Reclassified 2026-08-18 from closed_negative. The recorded -0.672 pts reproduces bit-for-bit, but it sits BELOW the instrument's own MDE80 of 0.927 pts (f=9.96%, n=9093), so it was never resolvable. Split-half reliability of the traits is 0.719 (dropback) and 0.680 (carry) on 1658/1671 team-seasons -- comparable to injury_value_lost's kept 0.87-0.93 and far above the 0.063/0.014 reliabilities that correctly closed other lines -- which rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability'. No positive control bounds this family (the +0.0129 MAE deliberate-leak control belongs to opponent adjustment, a different family, and was not borrowed). Neither admissible closing ground is met. A family-specific refit-aware bootstrap (measured inflation 1.438x, inside the documented 17-58% band) gives -0.078 pts P+ 0.367, converging with the sign-only read of -0.101.

cfb_travel_rest_eastbound_multizone.classification_evidence: Predeclared cross-league CFB replication (docs/cfb_body_clock_replication.md), frozen before scoring. The week-blocked 95% interval [-0.1949, +0.2233] crosses zero at this evaluator's resolution -- the EXPECTED shape for a real-but-small signal, never grounds to close per AGENTS.md. None of the three admissible grounds applies: (1) no resolved wrong sign, since the interval is not wholly on either side of zero; (2) no split-half reliability failure, since the underlying body-clock timezone trait reads Spearman-Brown 0.9928 and the near-zero per-cell exposure figure is arithmetic about how rare the schedule situation is rather than a trait measurement; (3) no positive-control bound, since the control PROVED detection only of a +48.4-point leak, which says nothing about a sub-0.3-point effect.
cfb_travel_rest_eastbound_multizone.description: CFB replication of NFL travel_rest_eastbound_multizone: this game's venue UTC offset minus the away school's own home-venue UTC offset >= 2 hours, both evaluated DST-aware at the game's own kickoff instant (the CFB table carries a UTC kickoff; the NFL version had to use gameday). Neutral sites excluded as NaN because no CFB venue-location field exists for them.
cfb_travel_rest_eastbound_multizone.notes: CLOSE-GRADED CFB: the CFB archive carries no verified opener (docs/cfb_data.md:42), so this is graded on the median-book close-proxy spread_line. A CFB result is replication evidence about a mechanism and never by itself changes an NFL card. No NFL evaluation window and no rotation window was spent. The four cells in family cfb_body_clock_replication are CORRELATED SUBSETS of one window and are NOT independent votes: east_host_west_visitor_early is a strict subset of west_road_early (24 of its 50 flagged games), night_west_road shares the identical body-clock definition at the opposite end of the kickoff distribution, and eastbound_multizone overlaps all three through the same timezone map. Never sign-test-pool them, and never pool them with the NFL siblings (different league, different grade, different baseline). Registered effect is the PRIMARY estimator: paired candidate-minus-baseline forced-pick accuracy delta, frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm (35 columns, ridge alpha 10, market-residual target, 500-game training floor, weekly refits trained strictly before each scored week) versus the identical estimator plus exactly this one column. Scored population 8,933 games / 199 week blocks / 13 seasons, with 271 neutral-site rows carrying NaN. Replicates NFL sibling travel_rest_eastbound_multizone (registry effect -0.1382, 95% [-0.7550, +0.4887], P+ 0.3239). Season-blocked secondary: 95% [-0.1448, +0.1682], P+ 0.612. SECONDARY NFL-COMMENSURABLE estimator (subset-vs-complement full-slate-scaled home_cover gap, scripts/_common.summarize, 20,000 draws): +0.0650 pts, week 95% [-0.1137, +0.2519], P+ 0.7599, season P+ 0.7593, n_flag 331, subset cover 51.06% vs complement 49.30%, raw gap +1.755 pts -- the OPPOSITE side of zero from the NFL sibling, so the NFL direction did not replicate. This is the only cell favoured on BOTH estimators. Flagged eastbound deltas: 213 games at 2 hours, 115 at 3, 7 at 4, 2 at 5, 1 at 6. Per-era primary magnitudes carry OPPOSITE SIGNS (2012-2019 +0.1122, P+ 0.780; 2021-2025 -0.1116, P+ 0.230), so the pooled number is an average across a sign flip -- both era slices are recorded separately. Instrument checks: within-week permutation null (200 draws) mean +0.021/-0.004/+0.030/+0.007 pts across the four cells, all centred within 0.03 points of zero; positive control (candidate column replaced by realised ats_margin) +48.405 accuracy points, P+ 1.000, 95% [+47.374, +49.464] on n=8,933 -- so the full 36-column ridge fit is not blind to a real effect of meaningful size. RELIABILITY FIELD carries the underlying body-clock UTC-offset trait: Pearson r 0.9858 95% [0.9843, 0.9871], Spearman-Brown 0.9928, n=2,420 team-seasons (odd/even-week split-half). The per-cell EXPOSURE propensities are, for the record: west_road_early SB 0.0990 (r 0.0521, 95% [-0.0121, +0.1966], P+ 0.6245); east_host_west_visitor_early SB -0.0075 (r -0.0037, 95% [-0.0060, -0.0019], P+ 0.0000); eastbound_multizone SB 0.5608 (r 0.3897, P+ 1.0000); night_west_road SB 0.7434 (r 0.5916, P+ 1.0000). For a per-team-season event that happens at most once, a positive in the odd half nearly always implies a zero in the even half, which forces a small negative odd/even correlation by construction, so the two thin cells' exposure figures measure RARITY, not the reliability of a trait. The AGENTS.md rationale for the no_split_half_reliability ground (no sample size rescues it) is false for a rare schedule fact, so that ground is NOT admissible for any cell in this family. Predeclaration: docs/cfb_body_clock_replication.md.

cfb_true_freshman_road_qb_on_benchmark.description: CFB true-freshman road QB fade (LEAD-47): unsigned flag backing home when the away team's post-hoc starter is a true freshman, on the frozen XLG-03 benchmark arm
cfb_true_freshman_road_qb_on_benchmark.notes: Flag cfb_lead47_true_freshman_road_qb_flag: 1 iff the AWAY team's post-hoc same-game starter (most dropbacks that game, via cfb_qb_dependence.build_cfb_qb_game_metrics, reused not rebuilt) is a true freshman by the 'first local roster-appearance-season' proxy (the local experience_years field is MEASURED to be frozen/static per athlete_id across seasons in this archive -- e.g. athlete_id 487698 reads experience_years==3.0 in 2018, 2019, AND 2021 alike -- and is not used; see docs/cfb_lead_screens_wave2.md). Population restricted to 2014-2019+2021-2025 (2012-2013 excluded: measured mean players/team-game 31.76/32.37 in 2012/2013 vs 105.51/112.14 in 2014/2015 confirms the stat-credited-only roster regime that cannot distinguish true from redshirt freshmen). 604 flagged of 7660 scored games / 168 weeks (away starter identified in 6818 of 7799 in-scope games, 87.4%; home true-freshman starters counted as a diagnostic, 657, never pooled into this flag). Positive control +48.460 pts P+ 1.000. Per-era: 2014-2019 -0.049 pts P+ 0.428 (week), 0.476 (season); 2021-2025 +0.251 pts P+ 0.889 (week), 0.952 (season) -- recorded separately, material divergence (sign flip, ~46-point P+ swing). Null clean: mean -0.003 pts, observed at the 69th percentile. Never pooled with XLG-06's recruiting-rating entries (no recruiting rating is read anywhere in this construct). Close-graded CFB; no NFL window spent or earned.

cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.classification_evidence: Week-blocked accuracy interval [-0.402,+0.208]pts crosses zero (P+=0.2491); season-blocked agrees ([-0.390,+0.227]pts, P+=0.2537). estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.classification_evidence: Own-model pick stability: single-fit pairwise flip rate (two individual bootstrap-refit draws disagreeing) 26.4% vs bagged split-half flip rate (mean of first 60 vs mean of second 60 of 120 refit draws disagreeing) 4.5% -- a 5.9x reduction, on 8,933 CFB games / 13 seasons. Accuracy: single-fit 51.14% vs bagged 51.31% (+0.17 pts, bagging beats the single fit). Bagged-vs-baseline (full-vs-thin) paired comparison: -0.168 acc pts [naive interval], P+ 0.383 (up from the single-fit arm's -0.336 pts / P+ 0.262 -- still crosses zero, so unresolved, but a genuine partial improvement in both estimate and P+ relative to not bagging). A DIRECT synthetic falsification attempt (fresh-bootstrap-of-a-training-resample own-model-instability design) found a null result instead (single flip 9.5% vs bagged 10.0%); diagnosed as a comparator design flaw (bootstrapping a bootstrap resample compounds variance rather than testing a fair 'fresh draw of history'), not evidence against the real-data finding. The real-data split-half design (splitting one clean bootstrap ensemble in half, no nested resampling) is the trustworthy comparator.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.description: Average predicted centres over training-row bootstrap-refit draws (bagging) instead of reporting a single point-estimate fit. Screened on the CFB thin-vs-full candidate comparison, reusing the refit draws already computed for the honest interval -- no extra fitting.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.notes: The flip-rate reduction (pick stability) is the strong, decisive part of this result; the accuracy/P+ improvement is real but modest and does not clear any promotion bar on its own. Recommend bagging as a default variance-reduction step for FUTURE candidate screens (it cannot move any current pick since it is not wired into any production path), not as a standalone accuracy claim. CORRECTION (recording agent, 2026-08-18): the drafted payload this entry is sourced from recorded effect=+0.17, which is sign-inconsistent with its own probability_positive=0.3825 and its own classification_evidence text ('-0.168 acc pts ... P+ 0.383'); +0.17 was actually the SEPARATE bagged-vs-single-fit accuracy delta (51.31% vs 51.14%), not the bagged-vs-baseline comparison this P+ describes. Recorded here as effect=-0.168 to match docs/estimation_variance.md sec 4a's literal 'Bagged vs. baseline, naive interval | -0.17 pts [naive], P+ 0.383' under this registry's positive-favours-candidate convention. The underlying finding (bagging helps, relative to the single fit) is unchanged by this correction; only the sign of the recorded full-vs-thin effect number is fixed.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.plain_summary: Method check: averaging many resampled model refits together.

estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.classification_evidence: Non-monotonic and noisy: shrink_fraction=1.0 (production strength) gives -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.255; 0.75 -> -0.448 pts P+ 0.181; 0.5 -> -0.414 pts P+ 0.208; 0.25 -> +0.034 pts P+ 0.543 (essentially zero, not a real flip, just the least-negative point); 0.0 -> -1.209 pts P+ 0.041. A matched synthetic check (linear DGP, location-biased residual sample, 100 replicates x n_boot=50) found the OPPOSITE, clean, monotonic pattern instead: shrink=1.0 always best (+1.67 pts, P+ 0.707), declining smoothly to shrink=0 (-5.52 pts, P+ 0.091). Flip-rate DOES fall monotonically with shrinkage in both the real and synthetic data (confirms the mechanism -- production's cover probability threshold is fixed against a nonzero-location residual sample, so uniform positive scaling is NOT sign-invariant, unlike coefficient scaling closed by MOD-06), but the real-data accuracy/P+ sweep does not replicate the synthetic monotonic decline, so there is no basis to claim a shrinkage sweet spot exists.
estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.description: Uniformly shrinking the predicted market-residual CENTRE (not the residual-sample READER, which residual_location.md already found inert) toward the market line by a fraction before reading the out-of-time residual ECDF. Screened on the thin-vs-full CFB comparison (market/context/experience-only baseline vs full CFB_MODEL_FEATURE_COLUMNS candidate).
estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.notes: Do not treat shrink=0.25's near-zero, barely-positive point estimate as a discovery -- it is the least-bad of five noisy negative-leaning arms, not a validated improvement. Recorded per AGENTS.md's binding rule (every category-3 result recorded, not discarded) precisely because it crosses zero, not because it looks promising. estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.classification_evidence: Ungated (tau=0): -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.264 (candidate LOSES to baseline). Gated at tau=0.05 (defer to baseline wherever the two arms' cover probabilities differ by <5 points): +0.246 acc pts, P+ 0.9505, f falls 19.8% -> 2.06% (MDE80 1.32 -> 0.43 pts). The sign flip and P+ jump REPLICATE independently on two disjoint season halves built by alternating clean-core seasons (scripts/estvar_f_lever_splithalf.py): half A (2012/14/16/18/21/23/25) P+ 0.399 -> 0.935 at tau 0->0.05; half B (2013/15/17/19/22/24) P+ 0.241 -> 0.744 at tau 0->0.05. Recorded unresolved rather than resolved because tau=0.05 was chosen from a 9-point sweep AFTER seeing the pooled result -- the split-half check supports the QUALITATIVE pattern (a modest disagreement gate makes this comparison provable) but not the specific tau or P+ figure at full precision; a predeclared tau on a train/validation split, confirmed once on a held-out test split, is required before this could be called resolved.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.description: Gate the 'full' CFB feature profile's influence to games where its predicted cover probability disagrees with the 'thin' (market+context+experience only) baseline by at least tau, deferring to the baseline elsewhere. Tests the general 'f lever' principle (MDE80 = 280*sqrt(f/n)): a surgical candidate that only moves the picks it has real information about is more provable than one that perturbs every pick.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.notes: This is a DETECTION-METHOD finding, not a new predictive feature -- 'full' and 'thin' are both already-existing profiles. The actionable implication is a general design principle for evaluating future candidates (gate influence to where the candidate disagrees with a simpler baseline), not a pick change. Do not promote or apply to any live model; this only screens the evaluator's own sensitivity. Recorded 2026-08-18 by a recording agent from docs/estimation_variance.md sec 5/sec 6 (the drafting session was barred from writing registry/*.json; this session verified the doc's tau=0.05 row and split-half table before recording, no fields required derivation).
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.plain_summary: Method check: model overrides baseline only where it clearly disagrees.

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.classification_evidence: Out-of-screen population (thin_2006_2011 minus 2006-2007, which fall below the 500-game training floor entirely under annual-refit cadence, + regime_2020): 2,533 games, 72 blocks. Real gate (tau=0.05, frozen, not re-swept): -0.316 acc pts, honest 95% interval [-1.323, +0.699] (refit_aware_interval, samples=20000), honest P+ 0.2733 -- crosses zero, does NOT directionally replicate clean-core's positive lean (P+ 0.9505 pooled, 0.935/0.744 split-half). Required placebo control (random gate, same n=411 membership count, seed 20260818): -0.553 acc pts, P+ 0.0512 -- worse than the real gate, which is evidence the disagreement selection is not arbitrary even though neither arm beats baseline here. Gate-membership reliability (120 paired refit draws): 23.09% overall flip rate under training-row resampling (1 - flip rate = 0.7691 recorded as reliability, converted to the registry's higher-is-better convention), 32.82% among point-fit in-gate games, 21.20% among out-gate games -- real instability, not enough alone to close as no_split_half_reliability. Realized f (7.03%) and membership rate (16.23%) are far above clean-core's ~2%, consistent with the flagged sparser-market regime confound (2a caveat 2) and not separable from it in this design. MDE80 at realized f/n is 1.47 pts, worse than the design's own 0.69-pt a-priori estimate and ~6x the original screen's +0.246-pt effect -- underpowered as expected, and the honest read is directional, not resolving, and leans negative rather than positive.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.description: Out-of-screen retrospective confirmation of the tau=0.05 f-lever disagreement gate (gate the CFB full profile's influence to games where it disagrees with the thin profile by >=0.05, deferring to thin elsewhere), frozen before this run per flever_scope/design.md. Tested against a required size-matched random-gate placebo control.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.notes: Confirmation run per flever_scope/design.md (2026-08-18), orchestrator adjudication: CFB-only (no NFL window drawn), no P+ bar applied to this methodology question, placebo arm required and run. Does NOT resolve or refute the disagreement-gate mechanism; the honest single-population read here is more cautionary than the design's hoped-for outcome (directional replication) -- point estimate and P+ both lean the WRONG way relative to clean-core on this specific out-of-screen population, though not to a resolved degree. The real-vs-placebo gap is the one piece of this run that leans toward the mechanism being non-arbitrary. Do not promote or apply to any live model.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.plain_summary: Confirmation: disagreement-gate idea retested against a random-gate placebo.

graph_off_rush_epa_on_production.classification_evidence: Close-graded per the predeclaration's grade discipline (mirrors scripts/graph_team_stat_record.py::classify): no terminal classification is drawn at this grade regardless of sign, and the binding 'grade the decision at the opener' rule means a close-graded look settles no play/no-play decision. On the week-blocked primary reference (within-week game correlation is zero by owner mandate) the CI upper bound is POSITIVE (+0.135), so the interval is not resolved entirely below zero and refuted_mechanism is unavailable. The season-blocked secondary CI [-1.195,-0.800] does sit wholly below zero, but with only 3 season blocks it has almost no combinatorial diversity and is a low-power artifact of block count, not a resolution -- and it is a secondary read at a grade that may not close anything. The positive control proved the harness can detect a large leaked effect (+48.999 pts) but did not bound whether an effect the size of the disjoint holdout's +1.996 reading would be reliably detected at this 749-game sample (the week-blocked CI spans about 2.1 points), so bounded_by_control is unavailable. Recorded unresolved_below_power.
graph_off_rush_epa_on_production.description: Graph ratings v2 team_stat off_rush_epa_per_play feature (signed-Katz opponent-adjusted, frozen CFB structure) stacked on PRODUCTION weak_stack/market_residual/ridge-alpha-10, versus production alone: does the family with the highest split-half reliability anywhere in this line of work (graph_input_screen_off_rush_epa_per_play, 0.987, opener-graded 2020-2025) add anything once measured on top of what is actually played?
graph_off_rush_epa_on_production.notes:
Paired candidate(weak_stack_graph_off_rush_epa)-minus-baseline(weak_stack) on 749 games, 51 weeks, close-graded 2014-2016 (rotation family graph_off_rush_epa_on_production, inherits graph_ratings_v2_team_stat; ASSIGNED the [2014,2016] block by nfl-ats rotation assign, never hand-picked -- the same block both sibling families drew, since a sibling's spent window is invisible to this family's own touched-season computation, disclosed in docs/graph_team_stat_off_rush_epa_on_production.md section 5). Candidate accuracy 50.07% vs baseline 51.00%. Week-blocked 95% CI [-1.998,+0.135] pts, P+ 0.037; season-blocked 95% CI [-1.195,-0.800], P+ 0.000 (degenerate, only 3 season blocks). Home-pick rate baseline 37.63% vs candidate 36.72% (close together, so little home-tilt artifact here). Within-week permutation null (200 perms, real feature) centres at +0.196 pts, sd 0.512; observed -0.935 sits at the 0.5th percentile of its own null -- the deepest negative-tail placement of the three siblings (off_sack_rate 6.0th, def_ypp 8.0th), though with 200 draws, three uncorrected families and no multiplicity correction, one tail placement is not itself a finding. Positive control (candidate column replaced by realized ats_margin) showed +48.999 pts, P+ 1.000, week 95% CI [+45.661,+51.921], proving the full-profile ridge harness is not blind. The paired delta is numerically identical to the off_sack_rate sibling's (-7 of 749 games) -- same window, same discrete grid, coincidence on the accuracy grid, not a shared computation. NOT commensurable with graph_ratings_v2_team_stat (bare-baseline comparator), graph_input_screen (single-feature vs zero-feature market baseline), graph_off_sack_rate_on_production or graph_def_ypp_on_production (different candidate families): the comparator here is the FULL PRODUCTION CHAIN, so this entry is NOT poolable with graph_ratings_v2_team_stat and is recorded under its own family per AGENTS.md's pooling-commensurability rule. CLOSE-graded: settles no play/no-play decision. Predeclared in docs/graph_team_stat_off_rush_epa_on_production.md before any outcome was scored, including the explicit prior that the screen doc calls this cell's apparent edge 'essentially all artifact'.

graph_team_stat_cfb_def_epa_per_play.description: CFB cross-league replication of the NFL graph team_stat arm, cell def_epa_per_play (stands in for the NFL def_yards_per_play cell; CFB has no yards-per-play column). Primary comparison: the frozen XLG-03 CFB market-residual benchmark arm (CFB_MODEL_FEATURE_COLUMNS, ridge alpha 10, 500-game training floor) versus the same arm plus one column, the signed-Katz differential of def_epa_per_play propagated over the CFB schedule graph at the NFL-frozen structure (alpha 0.85, half_life 8.0, max_row_l1 1.0, prior_weight 1.0, min_games 16, signed_katz, injury_beta 0.0). Graded at the benchmark own spread_line, XLG-03 clean core 2012-2019+2021-2025, walk-forward weekly refit. The raw diff_def_epa_per_play is ALREADY in the reference arm, so the graph is never credited for what the raw statistic earned. Benchmark accuracy 51.5952 pct, candidate 51.5840 pct.

hc_year_one_fade.classification_evidence: Era split is the whole question: clean 2009-2017 gap is +0.09 (n=391), mined 2018-2025 gap is -8.08 (n=465). The clean era REFUTES the -8 magnitude but NOT a moderate true effect -- a true -4 sits only 1.43 sigma from the clean-era observation, so it is not excluded. An earlier draft of this session called that a category-2 close; that was wrong and is corrected here. Escapes the closed coach-quality-reputation mechanism (reliability 0.063), which is a claim about a persistent coach TRAIT; this is an event/transition claim needing no stable trait. Not the team-quality ceiling either: invariant to quality by construction, and the gap survives inside the low-quality tercile (45.75% vs 51.46%).
hc_year_one_fade.description: First-year head coaches, weeks 1-8, cover below the kept-coach rate. Reproduced by two independent pipelines: 46.73% year-one vs 50.99% kept-coach on 856 games, gap -4.26 points.
hc_year_one_fade.notes: SCALE: the raw effect is a 4.26-point cover-rate gap on the 783 games (17.7% of the slate) with a first-year coach in weeks 1-8. Recorded on the FULL-SLATE scale so it is commensurable with feature-level accuracy deltas; an un-scaled subset effect would dominate any pool it entered. SIGN: the raw gap is negative (year-one coaches cover less); recorded positive because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the candidate HYPOTHESIS, which was exactly that they underperform. SIGN ORIENTATION: the raw cover-rate gap is -4.26 (year-one coaches cover LESS). Recorded as +4.26 because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the CANDIDATE HYPOTHESIS, and the hypothesis was exactly that they underperform -- the edge is exploitable by fading them. illness_home_ge2_on_production.classification_evidence: Close-graded look; per AGENTS.md's binding 'grade the decision at the opener' rule a close grade settles no play/no-play or terminal call regardless of sign, so unresolved_below_power is the only admissible classification here. Neither closing ground applies: no resolved wrong sign (the point estimate and both blockings favour the candidate) and no positive-control bound (the control detected +50.13 pts, proving the harness is not blind, but did not bound an effect of this size as absent).
illness_home_ge2_on_production.description: Home team illness_count >= 2 (injury-report illness designations, resolved as of that game's own pick deadline) added as ONE feature column on top of the FULL production weak_stack/market_residual/ridge/alpha-10 chain, versus production unmodified. Paired candidate-minus-baseline forced-pick accuracy delta on the rotation-assigned [2011, 2013] block, close-graded. Predeclared docs/illness_on_production.md; ranked #1 of four in docs/on_production_sweep_20260901.md.
illness_home_ge2_on_production.notes: Window [2011, 2013], 746 paired games, 51 weeks, close-graded, mode=screen. Production weak_stack accuracy 49.866% vs weak_stack_illness_home 50.134%; paired delta +0.268 accuracy points. Week-blocked (primary) 95% [-0.670, +1.230], P+ 0.662. Season-blocked secondary 95% [-0.398, +1.224], P+ 0.720 -- reported beside the primary, never averaged, and low-power with only 3 season blocks. Within-week permutation null (200 draws, real feature, unleaked) centres +0.082 pts, sd 0.621; observed sits at the 55.5th percentile of its own null -- essentially indistinguishable from its own null. Positive control (candidate column leaked to realized ats_margin) +50.134 pts, P+ 1.000 -- harness is not blind. Home-pick rate baseline 53.6% vs candidate 55.6%. This is the SPARSE arm as disclosed in the predeclaration before scoring: inside the window the column is non-missing on 99.87% of games but fires on only 4.30% (33 of 768), against 7.47% pooled over 2010-2024, so the ridge coefficient rests on ~33 firings. NOT POOLABLE with the bare-baseline illness battery (illness_home_ge2, comparator is a bare market baseline) nor with fluview_elevated_on_production (CDC regional ILI, different data source); AGENTS.md's commensurability rule forbids pooling across differing comparators and populations.

The realised-margin oracle control on the identical rows measured +45.9207 points, week-blocked 95% [+40.0911, +51.9139], probability_positive 1.000, so the instrument detects a large known effect but does not bound this approximately 1.4-point candidate effect. injury_value_lost_gradient.classification_evidence: Unchanged headline: the disagreement statistic resolves (rank-biserial +0.248 [+0.046,+0.450], p=0.016) but the ACCURACY effect does not (+1.75 [-0.69,+4.27], P+ 0.899) on the already-spent [2020, 2021] window, 456 games. NEW this session (docs/injury_value_lost.md): (1) split-half reliability of the underlying value-lost signal, measured on the full 2009-2025 history (4,431 games, 384 team-seasons, temporal odd/even-week split) is Pearson r=0.874 [0.843,0.901], Spearman-Brown corrected full-length reliability=0.933 [0.915,0.948], P+=1.000 (4000/4000 bootstrap draws) -- rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability' per AGENTS.md. (2) The RAPM-participation value-lost construct (M6, the family's one same-kind negative, -0.43 pts) has EQUALLY high reliability (0.860 raw / 0.925 corrected) -- so reliability does NOT explain M6's negative sign; more likely M6 tests the marginal value of a second, QB-inclusive, correlated value-lost construct stacked on top of one already in the model (full_player_participation = full_player_value + participation family), not whether value-lost as a concept works. (3) The mechanism-screen result survives a market-line-movement control unchanged (value_magnitude vs |close-open| line move: Pearson 0.029, near-zero; residualized disagreement rank-biserial 0.249 [0.047,0.451] p=0.016, statistically identical to the raw 0.248). (4) Survives dropping every QB-involved game: on the 397/456 games (87%) where neither presumed starter carried any listed injury, rank-biserial is still positive (+0.188 [-0.027,0.403], p=0.086) at comparable magnitude to the full sample -- consistent with the structural code finding that injury_skill_epa_value_lost deliberately zeroes QB rushing/receiving production (players.py:1260-1283), so this is provably not a QB proxy. (5) A methodologically CLEANER isolation exists and was run for the first time: player_value profile on game_features_player_value.parquet (built with FIXED-prior severity per its manifest player_feature_version=v2 tag, confirmed NOT learned) contrasted against the player baseline differs by ONLY the two value-lost columns -- zero semantics-shift confound, unlike this entry's original B-A contrast which mixed learned-severity semantics_shift into the same delta. That clean contrast gives +1.316 pts [-0.460,+3.247], P+ 0.8875, on the same 456 games, 26 disagreements (61.5% candidate win rate) -- smaller than +1.75 (removing the confound costs about a third of a point) but directionally intact. Recommend citing +1.316/P+0.8875 as the number to predeclare a narrowed family against, not the conflated +1.75 recorded here.
injury_value_lost_gradient.description: The availability/player-value half of the MOD-07 stack, whose gain concentrates in games with more injury VALUE lost rather than more availability-RATE shift. Tercile accuracy by value lost is monotone: -0.66 / +0.66 / +5.26 points.
injury_value_lost_gradient.notes: The narrowed candidate worth building: value-weighted injury magnitude with the learned-rate half dropped -- confirmed in docs/injury_value_lost.md section 4 using game_features_player_value.parquet (fixed severity) rather than the weak_stack table (learned severity), which removes the semantics-shift confound entirely. Predeclare as a new family `injury_value_lost_narrowed` inheriting mod07_weak_signal_stack (contaminates [2020,2021]); earliest eligible block after inherited contamination is [2022, 2023], one of only two remaining full opener blocks in the 2020-2025 pool. Do not assign until the 2026 prospective mod07_weak_signal_stack challenger (already ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE, artifacts/prospective/challengers.json) has produced its own number -- docs/injury_value_lost.md section 7 has the full predeclaration text to freeze verbatim. CFB cannot screen this family: value_lost requires a pregame injury-severity signal and none exists in any CFB source (docs/cfb_data.md, 'Availability semantics (fail closed)'); the nearest feasible CFB proxy (realized participation continuity, a different, postgame construct) already ran and lost (-0.67 pts on 8,933 games, cfb_role_continuity family, closed_negative).

injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence.notes:
Free re-read of the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] window; same 456 games, same D-A methodology as injury_value_lost_narrowed. Broader, report-independent population than injury_value_lost_prior_week_report (130,747 synthetic rows after schedule mapping vs 34,494) -- also catches non-injury roster-decision absences (healthy scratches, suspensions), a deliberate declared difference. Picks-disagreeing count differs from the report arm (17 vs 23), confirming the two arms are genuinely distinct model fits, not a duplicated construction, despite landing on the same aggregate accuracy by coincidence at n=456. Reliability of the underlying value-lost trait (0.87-0.93) was established on injury_value_lost_gradient's same-week construction, NOT independently re-measured for this construction -- left null here. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_official, injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_augmented, injury_value_lost_prior_week_report, mod07_opener_bias_ablation. kicker_change_underdog_on_production.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% CI [-1.3423, +0.8753] crosses zero -- the expected shape for a real small signal at this window size, not a resolved wrong sign. no_split_half_reliability is inadmissible: the construct is a deterministic text-pattern match over an already-captured point-in-time wire archive plus a published roster position fact, the same class of trait every prior wave's own reliability argument already covers for a text/schedule construct with no measurement-noise component. Positive control (candidate replaced by realized ats_margin) reads +44.298 accuracy points, week-blocked P+ 1.0 -- the harness is proven sensitive to an effect of that size before this screen result is read. Rare by construction (only 89/4902 full-schedule games ever flag) but recorded regardless, per the task's own instruction.
kicker_change_underdog_on_production.description: LEAD-16: kicker_change_underdog_flag stacked on production weak_stack, opener-graded, rotation window [2020,2021]. Signed +1 when the HOME team is the opener underdog and either team changed its kicker (confirmed signing/waiver-claim/PS-elevation/IR-activation of a kicker on the PFR transaction wire, wire-only, never post-hoc snap-count comparison), -1 when the AWAY team is the underdog, 0 otherwise. Population: 217 wire-resolved kicker-change events across the full local history (2016-2025), of which 89/4902 full-schedule games flag nonzero (all 2020+, since the Tuesday-opener spread store only covers 2020-2025).
kicker_change_underdog_on_production.plain_summary: Backing the underdog whenever either team just changed its placekicker, stacked on top of the production model, read essentially flat (-0.2 accuracy points, interval crossing zero) on a two-season opener test with only 27 games flagged in-window -- too rare and too close to zero to say anything yet.

mod06_js_shrinkage_position_prior_cfb.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% CI [-1.02,-0.04] accuracy points fully below zero (P+=0.017), 199 blocks >> RELIABLE_BLOCKS_FOR_INTERVAL=50; both old (SB=0.967) and new (SB=0.954) constructs clear split-half reliability decisively, ruling out no-reliability as the closing ground; Brier/log-loss point the same negative direction (P+=0.055 each); season-blocked (13 blocks, underpowered) is directionally consistent, point estimate identical, CI touches +0.02 at the very top. Reviewer adjudication 2026-08-18: terminal closure REFUSED despite the week-blocked interval sitting fully below zero -- re-crossing zero requires only a 1.082x widening (centre -0.53, upper -0.04), inside the documented 1.003-1.099x honest refit-correction band for fit-changing families (docs/estimation_variance.md Part II), and the season-blocked interval already crosses (+0.02 upper). Contrast offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb, whose closure needed 1.363x and was accepted. What is measured here is THIS construct at the untuned production alpha=10 (the screen's own flagged scale/collinearity confound), not the shrinkage mechanism.
mod06_js_shrinkage_position_prior_cfb.description: James-Stein unit-level shrinkage toward a position prior, vs. today's shrink-to-zero, applied to a new non-injury-gated CFB skill-unit-value feature (home/away/diff), screened against the frozen XLG-03 market_residual benchmark
mod06_js_shrinkage_position_prior_cfb.notes: Skill/offense-side only (defense-side CFB participant credits confirmed NOT wired into cfb_features.py canonical build); single accuracy arm per predeclaration (JS vs frozen baseline only, no OLD-construct accuracy arm); several underived constants reused from players.py (value_prior_snaps=200, value_span=16) plus new CFB-specific choices (QB_MIN_PASS_ATTEMPTS=5, JS_EPSILON=1e-4, MIN_EXPERIENCED_POOL=20) -- see script docstring for full list. Single-arm design: no direct old-vs-new accuracy comparison exists, only the reliability comparison (old 0.967 vs new 0.954, both high).
mod06_js_shrinkage_position_prior_cfb.plain_summary: Model setting: skill-value feature shrinks toward position average, not zero.

mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% paired interval on accuracy_improvement is [-0.444, +1.841] accuracy points, crossing zero. Per AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md an interval crossing zero is the EXPECTED shape for a real small signal at this evaluator's ~2pt resolution and is NOT grounds to reject; recorded per the binding taxonomy as unresolved, not closed. Season-blocked (8 blocks) agrees in direction (probability_positive 0.9524) but is flagged degenerate by experiments.paired_feature_comparisons's own guard, so only its point estimate is reported, not its interval.
mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping.description: Gaussian CDF read of the SAME out-of-time residual sample vs the production raw ECDF (margin._smoothed_probability), measured on the production weak_stack recipe (target=market_residual, ridge_alpha=10.0, min_train_games=500) restricted to NFL seasons no rotation-registry family has reserved. See docs/smooth_cdf_mapping.md.
mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping.notes: Non-reserved evaluation seasons (2009-2025 minus {2013-2017,2020,2021}, which are reserved by other rotation-registry families): 2009,2010,2011,2012,2018,2019,2022,2023,2024,2025 (10 non-contiguous seasons; season-start/end are the min/max, NOT contiguous coverage -- 2013-2017 and 2020-2021 were never touched by this measurement). Same protocol scores Brier and log-loss (both raw metric differences, positive=candidate better): brier_improvement +0.001861 [0.000871, 0.002868] P+ 0.9999; log_loss_improvement +0.004185 [0.002068, 0.006358] P+ 1.0000 (week-blocked, n=2047, seed 20260819, 20000 samples). Pick movement: 159/2111 games flip sides (7.53%), concentrated near pick'em lines (under_3 9.43%) and least common at the |line|=3 key number (4.80%), matching the mechanism and flip-rate magnitude already measured in docs/ecdf_smoothing.md's CFB/player-profile screen (7.4-7.9%). CONTRAST: the existing ecdf_smoothing_accuracy entry (CFB, player-profile screen) recorded accuracy leaning NEGATIVE (probability_positive 0.11); THIS entry (NFL, weak_stack production profile, non-reserved seasons) leans POSITIVE (probability_positive 0.8666) on the identical primary metric. Both are measured, from different leagues/profiles/windows; neither overrides the other. EV framing (AGENTS.md 'a promotion bar is not a decision bar'): P+ 0.8666 favours playing the Gaussian mapping on a per-pick EV basis even though the interval crosses zero; this measurement records that lean and feeds the smooth_cdf_mapping prospective challenger (artifacts/prospective/challengers.json) for continued no-window-cost 2026 evidence, but does not by itself change the default production mapping (margin._smoothed_probability stays bit-identical; promotion is the owner's/orchestrator's decision).
mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping.plain_summary: Model setting: bell-curve probability mapping vs the production method.

mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping_opener.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% paired interval on accuracy_improvement (production pick rule, settled at the opener) is [-1.397, +1.715] accuracy points, crossing zero -- per AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that is the EXPECTED shape for a real small signal at this evaluator's resolution and is NOT grounds to reject; recorded unresolved per the binding taxonomy. probability_positive 0.5536 is barely above a coin flip -- markedly weaker than the close-graded read on the SAME 1,537-game archive (probability_positive 0.8541) and than the full-history close-graded mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping entry (0.8666). This is the SECOND recorded look at this candidate's accuracy (multiplicity disclosed); the frozen decision rule in docs/smooth_cdf_mapping.md treats P+ > 0.5 as firing an EV-based promotion regardless of how close to 0.5 it lands, per AGENTS.md 'a promotion bar is not a decision bar' and 'grade the decision at the opener' -- so promotion fired on this result despite the weak margin.

See docs/smooth_cdf_mapping.md#opener-grade-decision-measurement.
mod08_smooth_cdf_mapping_opener.notes: Sign-rule diagnostic (mapping-invariance check, reported not gated): 0 flips between ecdf/gaussian arms at either the opener or close line for 1,537 games (sign rule never calls the probability-mapping function, so this is a structural fact, not a null finding); sign-rule opener accuracy 52.8277% and close accuracy 51.5594% both reproduce docs/opener_evaluation.md's tracked numbers exactly, confirming the script's weekly-refit protocol matches production. Brier/log-loss stay strongly positive at the opener grade too (brier_improvement +0.000723 P+ 0.9368; log_loss_improvement +0.001581 P+ 0.9488, week-blocked). Close-grade context on the SAME 1,537-game archive (secondary/informational, not the decision metric): accuracy_improvement +0.7963 points [-0.649, +2.262] P+ 0.8541. Season-blocked (6 blocks) flagged degenerate by paired_feature_comparisons's own guard; only its point estimate/P+ are meaningful (open accuracy P+ 0.5632, close accuracy P+ 0.8658).

mod17_joint_residual_realised_correlatio.classification_evidence: This entry is descriptive, not a candidate-vs-baseline comparison: there is no 'candidate' for a structural correlation between two residuals, so favours_candidate is not a meaningful read of this row. The season-blocked interval [0.0063, 0.0539] sits entirely above zero, but the effect is far too small (r^2 ~ 0.0009) to license any closing ground; recorded as unresolved_below_power because AGENTS.md's two closing grounds (resolved wrong sign; positive-control bound) do not apply to a descriptive measurement.
mod17_joint_residual_realised_correlatio.description: MOD-17 research half: Pearson correlation between the realised margin residual (ats_margin) and the realised total residual ((home+away)-total_line), the structural quantity behind the owner's question about a unified model
mod17_joint_residual_realised_correlatio.notes: docs/mod17_joint_residual_model.md predeclaration, part 1 (the structural quantity). Positive is stored as measured; there is no predeclared candidate-favouring direction for this descriptive entry -- see classification_evidence. Sets the ceiling on how much any joint-modelling scheme could ever gain from cross-target information (Part 3 of the same document); the controlled second-stage test in that document confirms letting the two models see each other's out-of-fold predictions does not beat simple own-shrinkage.
mod17_joint_residual_realised_correlatio.plain_summary: Games that beat the total by more also lean very slightly, but real, toward favouring the side the margin model already favours. The link is too small to build much on: even perfect knowledge of one residual could only explain about one part in a thousand of the other's variance.

mod17_joint_residual_total_blend.classification_evidence: Week-blocked bootstrap (2,000 resamples, seed 20260901) interval [-0.0066, +0.0165] is not wholly above/below zero on either side in the wrong direction, so wrong_sign_resolved does not apply; probability_positive 0.791 favours the candidate and meets the predeclared promotion bar (>0.5, non-negative point estimate), but a positive probability_positive is not itself a closing ground under AGENTS.md.
mod17_joint_residual_total_blend.description: MOD-17 research half: joint (union-feature, multi-output ridge) total-residual model, own MAE-minimizing blend weight, vs production served total blend (total_line + 0.1 x predicted_residual, wave-1 41-column allowlist)
mod17_joint_residual_total_blend.notes: docs/mod17_joint_residual_model.md predeclaration. Meets the predeclared EV promotion bar for the joint total output specifically (probability_positive > 0.5, non-negative point estimate); disclosed caveat: out-of-sample R2 vs the market is WORSE with the union feature set than with wave-1 alone (-0.0762 vs -0.0162), so this is not evidence of a real predictive improvement, only that a small, heavily shrunk (k=0.1) blend nudge happened to land better on this population. Promotion-style look on the reused population; no rotation window spent.
mod17_joint_residual_total_blend.plain_summary: Fitting the total model on a wider feature set (with the margin model's columns folded in) produced a slightly better total prediction than what is currently served, favoured about 4 times out of 5 in resampling. The underlying raw model fit is actually worse with more features; this small win survives only because the served number barely uses the raw model's signal.

mod18_conditional_margin_v1_oos1_w1_both.notes: Out-of-sample declaration of two post-hoc MOD-18 candidates: the atom set and the bucket set are chosen by a mechanical rule fixed in advance on the declaration seasons and graded only on later seasons the choice never saw. The declaration removes the discount on THAT CHOICE ONLY: the archive was mined by lanes H, K, L, R, S, T and U, the S3 baseline is itself a restriction fitted on it, the two cuts overlap in their declaration seasons and in 2023, and the three arms within a cut are nested and correlated. mod18_conditional_margin_v1_oos1_w1_both.plain_summary: Both changes at once. Football scores bunch up on a few numbers, so when the spread is set on exactly 7 points, this version reads the chance of covering from how often past games at a similar spread really finished on each score, and leaves every other game alone. Where the opening line is 10.5 points or more, the model's own disagreement with the betting number has been worth less than face value, so this version keeps only the share of it earlier seasons say is worth keeping, and leaves every other size of line exactly as it is played today. The choice was made by a fixed rule written down in advance, using only the 2020 to 2023 seasons. Measured on the 2024 to 2025 seasons, which the choice never saw. This row scores how close the stated chances were to what happened, not how many picks were right, and a positive number means the new way was closer.

This row counts the same thing after the usual weekly adjustments are applied to both.

mod18_home_side_location_v1_r2_r2_bucket.plain_summary: On the biggest lines the model's own disagreement with the betting number has been pointing the wrong way. This version works out from earlier seasons how much of that disagreement to keep at each size of line AND how firmly the record pins that amount down, so a size of line where the record is murky is left alone and only a clear pattern is allowed to change anything. This row reports how close the stated chances were to what happened, where a positive number means the new way was closer, on games where the opening line was 3 points or less.

movement_direction_tilt_opener.description: MOV-01 movement-direction forced-pick tilt, PRIMARY rule: flip the active weak_stack models opener pick to the movement-predicted side only when it disagrees AND predicted-move confidence is in the top half (median-split threshold computed from training-fold in-sample predictions only, never target-season data). Leak-free walk-forward reusing nfl_ats.clv.build_pilot_frame/fit_pilot_model/FROZEN_PILOT_FEATURES with no reimplementation of the model itself: seasons 2021-2023 each get a fresh expanding-window ridge refit trained only on strictly-earlier archived seasons (2021 trained on 2020 only; 2022 trained on 2020-2021; 2023 trained on 2020-2022); seasons 2024 and 2025 reuse the frozen MKT-06 pilot model AS-IS, trained once on 2020-2023 (FROZEN_PILOT_PROTOCOL), with no refit on either target season. Season 2020 excluded: no earlier archived season exists to train a leak-free direction model on. Effect and interval recorded here are OPENER-graded (project primary goal), week-blocked (90 week blocks, primary blocking). Joined population 1310 REG games, 2021-2025, against the active weak_stack opener-evaluation artifact; 59 of 276 opener-pick disagreements passed the confidence gate and were flipped.
movement_direction_tilt_opener.notes:
Close-graded secondary read (same opener-anchored decision, settled at the close line via pick_correct(home picks_at_open, margin_vs_close) -- deliberately NOT the active models own independently re-evaluated close arm, to keep the comparison apples-to-apples): delta -0.23 accuracy points, P+ 0.33 week-blocked / 0.30 season-blocked. Season-blocked bootstrap here uses only 5 blocks (2021-2025 seasons) -- thin, below the ~10-block reliability floor used elsewhere in this repo; read the week-blocked number as authoritative. Companion variants recorded separately: movement_direction_tilt_opener_variant1_no_filter (flip every disagreement) and movement_direction_tilt_opener_variant2_top_quartile (75th-percentile confidence gate).

DEFAULT_OFFSEASON_RETENTION=0.67 survives its audit.

pbp_trait_fourth_down_go_rate_reliabilit.classification_evidence: Reliability-only screen (lane J); this entry does not adjudicate a closing ground. Raw within-season Pearson r=+0.3145, 95% season-blocked CI entirely positive [+0.2074,+0.3828], P+=1.0000, Spearman-Brown full-length reliability +0.4785 -- the strongest raw reliability of the four screened metrics. CAVEAT (measured, not a reason to reclassify): unlike the other three metrics (whose label-shuffle nulls sit at +0.0001 to +0.0152), this metric's within-season null centers at +0.2059 (SD 0.0348) and its season-to-season null at +0.3096 (SD 0.0304) -- both far from zero. Because the null only shuffles team labels WITHIN a season, it cannot remove a trend that runs ACROSS seasons, and fourth-down aggressiveness has a well-documented leaguewide increase over 2009-2025; the raw r above is real and positive but likely conflates team-specific persistence with a shared era trend. The excess over the null (~+0.11 within-season, ~+0.10 season-to-season) is the more conservative read of team-specific persistence. Season-to-season replicate (not the recorded effect): r=+0.4124, 95% [+0.2760,+0.5012], P+=1.0000. A real filter bug (play==1 gate silently discarding all punts/FGs, giving a degenerate constant 1.0 go rate) was found and fixed before this measurement; see docs/pbp_trait_reliability.md and the pre-fix artifact kept at artifacts/pbp_trait_reliability/20260905T040022Z/results.json for the record. Earns an ATS look per the task's own bar (non-zero reliability, P+>0.5); ROADMAP LEAD-30 stays open pending the interaction-specific ATS look (BACK aggressive underdogs, FADE aggressive favorites -- never pooled).

NOT AN ATS NUMBER and NOT COMMENSURABLE with accuracy_points entries: this is a player-game availability metric on 52,382 rows, not a team-game ATS metric, and must not be pooled with ats/accuracy rows. Week-blocked bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260901, 174 week blocks; season-blocked agrees ([+0.0063044,+0.0090510], P+ 1.000). Log-loss agrees: +0.0281243 [+0.0254796,+0.0306238], P+ 1.000. POST-HOC DIAGNOSTICS (artifacts/per13_durability_stage1/20260901T191113Z/diagnostics.json, not part of the frozen comparison): a placebo that permutes each player's history to a random other player destroys the effect entirely (improvement -0.0000871), so the gain is row-level player information, not extra columns; prior-seasons-only history (no same-season rows) still yields +0.0038151, 51% of the effect, so about half is the multi-season trait PER-13 names and half is within-season recency; single-column gains run +0.0061778 (residual-vs-cell) down to +0.0004401 (reserve rate) with heavy redundancy, and only roster-absence (+0.00063) and history-depth (+0.00064) are uniquely irreplaceable. per13_durability_prior_availability_brie.plain_summary: Some players miss more games than their injury-report status suggests, and some play through it. play_probability_model_brier_improvement.description: Walk-forward, isotonic-calibrated HistGradientBoostingClassifier P(player plays) vs the current lineup-panel base-rate approach (nfl_ats.lineup_availability's no-designation rate by position group + recent role, plus the fixed injury-status prior for listed players), evaluated on 361,176 depth-chart-row-weeks across 12 walk-forward test seasons (2014-2025), each scored by a model trained only on strictly earlier seasons. Effect is the serving-realistic ablation (roster_status forced to ACT in both training and testing, matching the deployed default when the current week's live roster/inactive designation is not yet published) -- the conservative, deployment-representative number, not the full-information training-time Brier (0.181 improvement) which leans partly on the historical INA/roster-status column not normally available at serve time.
play_probability_model_brier_improvement.notes: Full-information (true historical roster_status available) Brier improvement vs the same current-approach baseline: 0.181 [0.175, 0.188]. Vs the depth-rank-only baseline (position_group + depth_rank_bucket, season-lagged shrinkage), serving-realistic improvement: 0.077 [0.068, 0.085]; full-information: 0.135 [0.118, 0.148]. Model overall Brier 0.040 (full-information) / 0.099 (serving-realistic) vs depth-only baseline 0.176 and current-approach baseline 0.221. Calibration table (mean predicted vs observed by slot, full-information run): QB1 0.830/0.820, QB2 0.270/0.249, QB3+ 0.080/0.088, RB1 0.821/0.820, WR1 0.817/0.821, OL 0.718/0.721, DL 0.764/0.773, LB 0.790/0.790, CB 0.750/0.748, S 0.799/0.800, K/P 0.878/0.879 -- all gaps under 0.02 except WR4+ (+0.038) and 'other' (+0.023, small-n K/P-adjacent bucket). Secondary 'started' label (snap share >= 50% of a player's own specific-position bucket that game, or being the depth-chart QB1 who actually played) is far coarser: measured started rates by rank-1 position range from ~0.4% (CB, 2-3 simultaneous corners) to ~82% (QB); documented in docs/play_probability_model.md as a known limitation of the literal task-specified proxy, not a code defect.
play_probability_model_brier_improvement.plain_summary: A real per-player forecast model that looks at depth-chart rank, this week's injury report, and recent playing time beats the lineup panel's old flat position-based guess by about 12 Brier points (0.124, 95% season-blocked interval 0.102 to 0.146) at predicting whether a listed player takes a snap, even after removing the one input (this week's official inactive list) that usually is not available yet when the panel is built.

player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.classification_evidence: Reclassified 2026-08-18 from refuted_mechanism. The prior refutation stated the two arms 'differ only in ridge alpha (1 vs 10)'; that is factually wrong about THIS entry, whose arms (candidate, base_alpha1) are BOTH alpha=1 and differ only in feature set (measured: predictions.parquet ridge_alpha is 1.0 for both). The near-null-contrast and 0.03%/0.27% shrinkage argument belongs to the SEPARATE alpha-only contrast base_alpha1 vs base_alpha10, which flips only 25/997 picks (2.51%) and is resolvably negative. This feature contrast flips 177/997 (17.75%), split 94-83, paired SE 1.33 pts, MDE80 3.74 pts. The prior evidence also compared a PAIRED delta against an UNPAIRED coin-flip sd (1.58), overstating noise. The two +-1.1033 figures are independent measurements that cancel by algebraic identity (candidate minus base_alpha10 = 0), not one number explaining the other. No split-half reliability was ever measured for the trait and no family-specific positive control exists, so neither admissible closing ground is met.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.description: QB + lineup continuity features, compared at MATCHED regularization (both arms ridge alpha=1); only the feature set differs.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.notes: Window [2014, 2017] remains permanently SPENT; only the interpretation of the spent look changes. sample_blocks switched 4 -> 68: the recorded [0.0, 2.2177] was season-blocked on exactly 4 blocks, on the documented degeneracy floor with a lower bound of exactly 0.0. The 68-week-blocked interval on the identical 997 games is the trustworthy one. Actionable reading unchanged and now better supported: the features want less regularization than the rest of the design, which points at group-wise ridge penalties.

pt_post_mnf_sunday_changepoint.notes: Predeclared in docs/era_mechanism_screens_20260901.md section 2.2 BEFORE any effect was computed; proposed unrun in docs/era_magnitude_report.md section 2.2. Located break season 2019 (bootstrap median 2019, 95 percent spread [2012, 2023]); pre-break mean +0.2550 [-0.1324, +0.6470] P+=0.8997, post-break mean -0.1874 [-0.6335, +0.2624] P+=0.2084. The batterys FIXED 2017/2018 convention on the same series gives pre +0.2557 / post -0.1329, gap -0.3886 [-0.9786, +0.2046] P+=0.0969 - the fixed convention and the free break agree to within 0.05 points, so the fixed boundary was not in the wrong place. Within-week permutation null (200 draws): the free-break magnitude null is centred near zero (-0.0157) with spread [-1.0283, +1.0267] and 65.5 percent of null draws have |magnitude| at or above the observed |0.4424| - an optimal changepoint estimator manufactures a break this large from a shuffled label most of the time; the fixed-convention gap fares better (21.5 percent). SEASON-BLOCKED SECONDARY IS STRUCTURALLY DEGENERATE for this metric and carries no information: a season-block resample of a per-season-series statistic reproduces the same series every draw, collapsing the interval to a point - reported for completeness only. DISCLOSED OVERLAP: same rows as pt_post_mnf_sunday and its two era arms; correlated, never an independent vote. Mined-window discount applies. n_flag 586 of 8090 eligible.

qb_news_backup_visible_by_deadline_scree.notes:
Revives backup_qb_fade_overlay (killed dead-on-arrival in docs/prospective_evidence.md: schedules.parquet QB-name columns are post-game-only) via timestamped PFT (299,739 urls, docs/injury_news_sourcing.md) + PFR-transactions (72,368 urls, docs/pfr_transactions_sourcing.md) news corpora, per owner correction 2026-08-20 that picks are editable up to each game's own deadline = min(kickoff, that week's Sunday 16:00 ET), not just Tuesday noon. Ground truth: 916 backup starts / 4588 eligible (>=3 prior starts) team-games, 2015-2025, identical construct to bias_battery_backup_qb_start. Visibility (matching rule + buckets frozen in docs/qb_news_channel.md before any cover rate was seen; QB full name + a 64-keyword injury/start/bench/roster-move list, both corpora, 10-day lookback anchored on the deadline): 26.31% by Tuesday noon, 39.96% cumulative by Friday, 44.98% cumulative by Sunday 10am ET-or-deadline (this screen's flag), 47.27% cumulative before the deadline, 52.73% never -- vs. the 2.39%-by-Tuesday-noon comparator for the official Wed-Fri injury report alone (docs/injury_news_sourcing.md sec 5.1), an ~11x improvement from using outlet news instead of the mandated report. Flag = backup start AND news-visible by that bucket; complement = every other eligible team-game. Sign=+1 matches bias_battery_backup_qb_start's own convention exactly (comparable without a flip).
