redzone_third_down_over_fade_on_producti.classification_evidence: Close-graded look; per AGENTS.md's binding grade-at-the-opener rule a close-graded run settles no play/no-play decision and cannot carry a terminal classification regardless of sign. Neither admissible closing ground applies: the sign is POSITIVE (so no wrong_sign_resolved), the trait's split-half reliability is 0.407 with 95% CI [+0.337,+0.473] (so no no_split_half_reliability), and the positive control proved the instrument CAN see an effect (+50.134 pts, P+ 1.000) but did not prove it would reliably resolve an effect of this size on 746 games (so no positive_control_bound). Reported as probability_positive, never as a binary interval statement.
redzone_third_down_over_fade_on_producti.description: Third-down mean-reversion fade (redzone_reversion_screen C3) as ONE game-level column redzone_third_down_over_fade_diff = int(home flagged) - int(away flagged), stacked on the PRODUCTION weak_stack / market_residual / ridge alpha 10.0 chain and compared against that chain unmodified. Close-graded, rotation-assigned window [2011, 2013], paired forced-pick accuracy delta.
redzone_third_down_over_fade_on_producti.notes: Window [2011,2013], --mode screen, ASSIGNED by nfl-ats rotation assign (never hand-picked); family declared with no --inherits (the reversion battery holds no rotation family) and no --acknowledge-mined (block does not intersect 2018-2025). Instrument checks ran FIRST, in order. Within-week permutation null (200 draws, real feature): centre +0.172 pts, sd 0.666, 95% [-1.206,+1.344]; the observed +0.670 sits at the 74.5th percentile of that null. Positive control (candidate column replaced by realized ats_margin): +50.134 accuracy points, week-blocked P+ 1.000, 95% [+46.428,+53.652], 100.0th percentile of its own null -- the full-profile ridge fit is not blind. Home-pick rates: baseline 53.646%, candidate 56.120% (2.47-point gap; this is what pushes the null off zero, and the percentile reading is the null-adjusted number). Baseline accuracy 49.866% vs candidate 50.536% on 746 paired games / 51 weeks. Season-blocked secondary [+0.000,+2.000], P+ 0.672, reported beside the week-blocked primary and never averaged with it; only 3 season blocks. Column distribution INSIDE the window: coverage 100.000% of 768 games, -1 on 18.750% (144), 0 on 62.500% (480), +1 on 18.750% (144), non-zero on exactly 37.500%. TWO DECLARED DEVIATIONS from the registered cell, both frozen in docs/redzone_reversion_on_production.md section 2 before scoring: (1) the team-game cell becomes one signed game-level difference, preserving C3's direction (a home over-performer to fade is +1) and collapsing both-flagged and neither-flagged to 0; (2) the top-quartile threshold is recomputed EXPANDING over strictly prior seasons only, replacing the frozen screen's whole-panel 2009-2025 quantile (a mild look-ahead a pregame column may not carry) -- a noisier threshold can only attenuate toward the null. NOT POOLABLE with the bare-baseline reversion battery (redzone_reversion_c1..c6): same trait, non-commensurable comparators (subset cover-rate gap vs a bare market baseline versus a paired forced-pick accuracy delta vs the full production chain) and different populations after deviation 2; AGENTS.md's commensurability rule forbids combining them.

ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation.classification_evidence:
PRIMARY (opener grade, n=1,537 paired games, 107 weeks, 2020-2025): baseline 52.83% vs candidate 51.43%, paired candidate-minus-baseline delta -1.397 pts, week-blocked 95% CI [-3.15, +0.27] pts, P+ 0.0504; season-blocked 95% CI [-2.69, +0.26] pts, P+ 0.0429. The upper bound of both intervals still crosses zero, so per AGENTS.md's binding rule this stays unresolved (category-3), not refuted, despite a ~95-96% lean against the candidate.
SECONDARY (close grade, same paired games; per AGENTS.md this may never veto the opener-graded primary and did not need to): delta -0.332 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.350, season-blocked P+ 0.294 -- same direction, much weaker, closer to genuinely unresolved.
CALIBRATION DIRECTION (Brier/log-loss, same opener-graded paired games): improves in the candidate's favor, P+ 0.77-0.90 across week/season blocking (Brier P+ 0.771 week / 0.862 season; log-loss P+ 0.802 week / 0.895 season). On the separate nflverse_spread full-history grade (2,075 games, 2018-2025) this direction resolves outright at season-blocking: Brier P+ 0.9995, log-loss P+ 1.000.
MULTIPLICITY: alpha=2,000 was pre-localized on the CFB instrument by two predeclared grids (13-point coarse log-grid 1e-3-1e5, then a 6-point refinement after the coarse Brier curve turned over near 1,000-3,000), both already recorded in docs/ridge_alpha.md and the ridge_alpha_global registry entry. This NFL run is one confirmation look at that already-localized value on a different instrument, not a search -- no alpha grid was swept here, no alternative candidate was tried.
CROSS-INSTRUMENT SIGN DISAGREEMENT: CFB's own accuracy screen at this alpha leans positive for the candidate (+0.258 pts, P+ 0.756 week / 0.711 season, docs/ridge_alpha.md), while this NFL opener-graded look leans negative (P+ 0.04-0.05) and the NFL nflverse-graded look also leans negative but less decisively (P+ 0.16-0.23). The two instruments disagree on accuracy's sign while agreeing on Brier/log-loss's sign -- consistent with docs/ridge_alpha.md sec2b's reading that the accuracy curve's apparent bumps are noise scatter around a genuinely flat surface rather than a real effect.

ridge_alpha_global.classification_evidence: Week-blocked interval contains zero (P+ 0.758); season-blocked P+ 0.703, also unresolved. This is a SECOND LOOK: alpha=2,500 was chosen after a coarse 13-point predeclared grid (1e-3..1e5) showed the Brier curve turning over near 1,000-3,000, then a 6-point refinement grid localized the minimum. The refinement narrows a point estimate; it does not license a stronger claim than the coarse grid already supports (coarse alpha=3,000: accuracy +0.213 pts, P+ 0.716/0.659; Brier +0.000294, P+ 0.933/0.894). The Brier half IS resolved and consistent across the whole 300-10,000 band (all P+ >= 0.75, most >= 0.93), which is the resolvable companion result -- see notes.
ridge_alpha_global.description: Global ridge penalty (market_residual / weak_stack, CFB walk-forward screen, 2,000-alpha grid) vs the frozen production alpha=10. Brier/log-loss improve with high confidence in a broad 300-10,000 band (peak near 2,000-2,500); forced-pick accuracy does not move.
ridge_alpha_global.notes: Blocked behind: the active production model runs alpha=10, which shrinks the median principal direction of the fitted design by only 0.27% (docs/ridge_alpha.md sec 1) -- i.e. alpha does essentially nothing on the ~70 well-conditioned, signal-bearing directions and is not chosen with any bias-variance tradeoff in mind. Accuracy is flat across [0.001, 10000], a 7-order-of-magnitude range, with no candidate clearing P+ >= 0.90 on both week- and season-blocking. Route the Brier gain to the Best Pick ranker (docs/pool_edge_plan.md queue item 2), not to a production accuracy swap. Do not pool this with groupwise_ridge_block_penalties without checking commensurability -- different mechanism (global penalty level vs. per-block allocation), though both are ridge-penalty-structure findings on the same CFB instrument with the same accuracy/Brier split pattern.

road_fav_big_fade_on_production.classification_evidence: Opener primary (week-blocked, production rule): -1.5351 accuracy points, 95% CI [-2.8634, -0.2188], P+=0.00785 -- the WHOLE interval sits below zero at both week-blocking (35 blocks) and season-blocking (2 blocks, same sign). wrong_sign_resolved is admissible: this is a RESOLVED wrong sign, not merely a lean. This is the symmetric on-production stack docs/schedule_flag_battery.md 'Wave 3' predeclares (task-instructed extension of lane G's one-sided public_claim_road_fav_big_fade claim, which only tested fading the road favorite). Ablation (measured, not separately recorded): isolating either half alone (away-big-favorite only, or home-big-favorite only) crosses zero individually -- the resolved negative is a property of the POOLED symmetric column, an instance of AGENTS.md's own pooling-can-transform-a-result principle realized in the negative direction. The sign-rule read on the identical population leans the OPPOSITE way and crosses zero (P+ 0.94185) -- a disclosed secondary diagnostic, not decisive (AGENTS.md: grade at the opener using the production rule). This refutes the ON-PRODUCTION STACK specifically; lane G's original close-graded public_claim_road_fav_big_fade cell remains its own unresolved_below_power entry and is not reclassified.

roof_battery_closed_benign_forecast_vs_o.notes:
schedules.parquet's own temp/wind fields are ~100% NaN for every retractable-venue game regardless of roof state (measured) -- the only local source with an independent pregame forecast at the stadium's own coordinates is data/raw/forecast_archive/full_2020_2025/forecasts.parquet (NDFD/GFS-MOS, 100% populated for both open/closed retractable games in that table). n_flag=145 closed-and-benign games out of 3,164 team-game rows in the 2020-2025 window. Side count (anecdotal, NOT bootstrapped, too rare to test): 9 games where roof was OPEN despite a non-benign forecast. Operational timing: the benign/non-benign FORECAST classification is itself Tuesday-safe (NDFD/GFS-MOS forecasts are available days ahead), but the cell as a whole is still gated on the actual roof OUTCOME, which is only known ~T-90min before kickoff (footballzebras.com policy explainer) -- so this cell stays kickoff-adjacent overall, playable via the refresh pass, NOT usable at the Tuesday lock, despite the Tuesday-safe weather half.

roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed.notes:
Retractable population (measured, data-driven): home_team in {ARI,ATL,DAL,HOU,IND} AND roof in {open,closed}, n=626 REG games 2009-2025 before push-dropping. ATL restricted to its Mercedes-Benz Stadium era (2017+) automatically since pre-2017 Georgia Dome games are tagged 'dome', not open/closed. rookie_crew_served_step_flagged_games_ca.plain_summary: When the referee working a game is in his first or second season, back the side the model likes once it knows that. Over 2020-25 this changed 3 of our picks and moved us from 56.9 percent to 57.0 percent right against the opening line -- about 71 percent likely to be an improvement, which is small and not settled, but better than a coin flip. This week it applies to exactly one game.

rookie_wall_dependence_reliability.classification_evidence: Both split-half schemes' full bootstrap interval sits entirely positive and both clear their team-label shuffle null (percentile 1.000 and 0.993), but reliability alone is never one of AGENTS.md's two admissible closing grounds (wrong-sign-resolved or positive-control-bound) -- this records the metric's measured reliability for a later ATS lane to build on, not a closed effect.
rookie_wall_dependence_reliability.description: LEAD-24 Stage 1: split-half reliability of the team-week top-50-pick-rookie snap-dependence metric (share of a team's offense+defense snaps taken by top-50-pick rookies). Odd/even-week within-season correlation across 416 team-seasons (2013-2025), Spearman-Brown corrected. A second, independent season-to-season scheme (team-level year-over-year persistence, n=384 team-season pairs, block=earlier season) reads Pearson r=0.129, 95% CI [0.044, 0.225], P+ 1.0, shuffle-null percentile 0.993 -- also fully positive and outside its own team-label shuffle null.
rookie_wall_dependence_reliability.plain_summary: Which teams lean hardest on high-draft-pick rookies is a real, stable team trait, not week-to-week noise: a team's rookie-dependence in the first half of its games nearly matches the second half of the same season (correlation 0.99), and even carries over, more modestly but still measurably, into the following season.

score_lattice_closest_total.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice's MEDIAN total vs the shipped tiebreaker's weighted-median total: paired absolute error against the realised total, walk-forward 2012-2025, identical neighborhood and centre. score_lattice_closest_total.notes: Declared as metric (c) in docs/score_lattice.md section 1.4 before the run; disclosed plainly that section 1.6 named only three registry rows and this is a fourth, added so a resolved POSITIVE result is not the one left unrecorded. Not wired into production: the pool's tiebreak metric is not recorded anywhere in this repository, and this session's frozen decision rule hung on the exact-score metric only.
score_lattice_closest_total.plain_summary: For the closest-total version of the tiebreak, sliding old games onto this game's exact line gives a total that lands about a quarter of a point closer, every week, than the current method. Same idea that hurt the exact-score guess helps here.

score_lattice_log_loss.classification_evidence: Resolvably POSITIVE (whole interval above zero), so no closing ground applies and none is claimed; recorded as category 3 because the enum has no 'resolved positive' state. The gain is attributable, and the attribution is disclosed rather than buried: the comparator assigns zero weight to the realised final in 55.1% of games, and on the 44.9% where it is alive the lattice is resolvably WORSE (-1.946 [-2.086, -1.807], probability_positive 0.0000). The honest reading is that a mode list is not a probability distribution, not that the lattice is sharper.
score_lattice_log_loss.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice vs the shipped tiebreaker mode list: paired log loss on the realised exact final, walk-forward 2012-2025, both arms smoothed identically by one pseudo-observation spread over the same data-derived feasible support. Positive favours the lattice
score_lattice_log_loss.notes: Predeclared docs/score_lattice.md section 1.4 including the restricted-support diagnostic that produced the attribution above. Smoothing scheme is one pseudo-observation over |S|, applied by the same formula to both arms.
score_lattice_log_loss.plain_summary: The lattice can put a number on any final score; the shipped list of common finals can only name three and says nothing about the rest. Scored as a probability the lattice wins easily, but only because its rival is silent more than half the time -- where both speak, the lattice is the worse of the two.

score_lattice_top1_exact.classification_evidence: Interval contains zero, which is never grounds to reject. The positive control (oracle_total arm, same instrument, same 3,829 games) moved top-1 by +6.35 points [+5.55, +7.12], so the instrument is PROVEN able to detect a 6-point effect but was never proven able to detect a 0.2-point one -- bounded_by_control is therefore unavailable and this is category 3.
score_lattice_top1_exact.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice vs the shipped tiebreaker mode list: paired per-game top-1 exact-final hit rate, walk-forward 2012-2025, both arms sharing the identical kernel-weighted neighborhood and centre; candidate recentres each neighborhood game by its (margin, total) market residual and interpolates onto the integer score lattice
score_lattice_top1_exact.notes: Predeclared docs/score_lattice.md section 1 before any outcome number. Decision rule was: switch the tiebreaker's exact-score section to the lattice if probability_positive > 0.5. It is 0.0615, so tiebreaker.py was NOT changed.
score_lattice_top1_exact.plain_summary: Guessing the exact final score by shifting old games onto this game's line, instead of just counting the most common finals in similar games, hits the exact score 0.42% of the time against 0.63% -- a fifth of a point worse, with too much noise to call it settled.

score_lattice_top3_exact.classification_evidence: The whole week-blocked 95% interval [-1.636, -0.689] sits below zero on 3,829 paired games across 299 week blocks, so the sign is RESOLVED wrong -- the admissible wrong_sign_resolved ground, not an interval-contains-zero rejection. Mechanism refuted as stated: recentring by the market residual smears exactly the score lumpiness the top-3 product lives on, which docs/score_lattice.md section 1.2 predicted in writing before the run. Confirmed independently by the declared secondary arm: without recentring the lattice reproduces the mode list cell for cell (delta exactly 0.000), so the entire loss is the recentring and none of it is the smoothing.
score_lattice_top3_exact.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice vs the shipped tiebreaker mode list: paired per-game any-of-top-3 exact-final hit rate, walk-forward 2012-2025, identical neighborhood and centre in both arms
score_lattice_top3_exact.notes: Predeclared docs/score_lattice.md section 1. Refutes the top-3 correct-score product of the residual-recentred lattice, NOT the lattice's other products: on the same run its median total beat the shipped closest-total answer by 0.263 total points [+0.162, +0.366] and it supplies P(push), which a mode list cannot produce at all.
score_lattice_top3_exact.plain_summary: Listing three likely exact final scores works better the plain way -- count the most common finals among similar games -- than by sliding old scores onto this game's line first. The sliding blurs the scores football actually produces, and it costs about 1.2 hits per 100 games.

surface_familiarity_r1_turf_venue_visito.classification_evidence: An interval or CI that contains zero is NEVER grounds to reject, fail, or close an experiment. At this evaluator's ~2-point resolution, contains zero is the EXPECTED outcome for a real small signal. Only two grounds ever close a line of work: (1) refuted mechanism -- a RESOLVED wrong sign (whole interval on the wrong side of zero) or zero split-half reliability; (2) bounded by a positive control proven able to detect an effect that size. Everything else is unresolved_below_power. Week-blocked 95% CI [-0.477,+3.366] crosses zero -- expected shape, not grounds to close. No admissible closing ground applies: wrong_sign_resolved requires the WHOLE interval on the wrong (negative) side and this interval's upper bound is +3.37 (predicted/positive side); no positive-control bound was run. Follow-up on a mined weather-battery cell (multiplicity already spent upstream), so recorded unresolved_below_power regardless of shape, matching the parent entry's own precedent.
surface_familiarity_r1_turf_venue_visito.description: Venue-controlled follow-up on weather_battery_surface_switch_grass_to_turf (registry), which conflated turf venue with grass-modal visitor. WITHIN turf-venue REG games only (surface_norm=='turf'), grass-modal-home visitor (mismatched, n=1112, home_cover=0.5225) vs turf-modal-home visitor (matched, n=745, home_cover=0.4886); raw gap +3.389pts, fraction_of_slate 0.4302 (n_pair 1857/4317), full-slate effect +1.458pts. totals_market_residual_blend.description: Ridge on the market total's residual (total_residual = home_score + away_score - total_line), 41-column frozen allowlist, SimpleImputer(median,+indicator) -> StandardScaler -> Ridge(alpha=10), expanding walk-forward by (season, week) with min_train_games=500. Effect = mean per-game reduction in absolute total error from serving total_line + 0.1 * predicted_residual instead of the market total alone, on 3935 regular-season games 2010-2025.
totals_market_residual_blend.notes:
SIGN CONVENTION: effect is stated as an IMPROVEMENT, so POSITIVE IS BETTER -- it is (market mean |error|) minus (blend mean |error|) in total points, +0.00082 here. This is the opposite of the raw 'mae' unit's usual negative-is-better reading; --effect-units mae was chosen because it is the only supported unit measured in points of absolute error (the unit actually wanted was 'total_points_mae_improvement', which the recorder does not offer). Raw levels for reference: market total MAE 10.4249, chosen blend (k=0.1) MAE 10.4241, raw model total (k=1.0) MAE 10.5495 -- the raw model total is WORSE than the market, the same shape the margin side found. MAE-minimising k over {0.0..1.0} is 0.1; alphas 1 and 100 also pick k=0.1 (+0.0009, +0.0012). Playoffs reported separately, never pooled: 188 games, market MAE 10.9231, blend MAE 10.8994, delta +0.0237. Per-season deltas split 9 positive / 7 negative. Interval is a week-blocked bootstrap (nfl_ats.clv.week_blocked_bootstrap, 2000 resamples, 261 week blocks, seed 20260901). Wired as nfl_ats.tiebreaker.TOTALS_RESIDUAL_WEIGHT = 0.1.

totals_market_residual_blend.plain_summary: We built a model to guess whether a game goes over or under the posted total, then checked it week by week against every season since 2010. On its own it is worse at guessing the final total than the betting line is. Nudging the line 10% of the way toward the model is very slightly better than using the line alone -- about eight thousandths of a point per game -- so the tiebreaker guess now takes that small nudge.

totals_market_residual_wave2_vs_wave1.description: Wave 2 of the totals residual regime: wave 1's 41-column ridge allowlist plus 24 drive-pace columns ({home,away} x points/yards/plays/seconds per drive, scoring/turnover/takeaway rate, from data/processed/game_features_pbp.parquet), same pipeline (SimpleImputer(median,+indicator)->StandardScaler->Ridge(alpha=10)), same expanding walk-forward (min_train_games=500). Effect = paired per-game |error| improvement of the wave-2 blend (own MAE-minimizing k=0.1) over the wave-1 blend (frozen k=0.1), on the identical 3935 regular-season games 2010-2025 both waves score.
totals_market_residual_wave2_vs_wave1.notes: SIGN CONVENTION: positive = wave 2 better (wave-1 |error| minus wave-2 |error|), matching totals_market_residual_blend's convention. Raw levels: market MAE 10.4249 (identical to wave 1's, confirming identical population), wave-1 chosen blend (k=0.1) MAE 10.4241, wave-2 chosen blend (k=0.1, its own sweep minimum, matches wave 1's operating point by coincidence not by construction) MAE 10.4221, wave-2 raw model (k=1.0) MAE 10.5799 (worse than market, same shape as wave 1's own raw model at 10.5495 and the margin side). Wave-2 vs market alone: MAE improvement +0.0028 (secondary metric), about 3.5x wave 1's own +0.0008 vs-market figure. Per-season paired MAE deltas (wave1_mae - wave2_mae, positive = wave2 better): 10 of 16 seasons positive, 6 negative; 2010 (16-game warm-up stub) is the largest negative outlier at -0.0774, all other seasons within +-0.02. Interval is a week-blocked bootstrap (nfl_ats.clv.week_blocked_bootstrap, 2000 resamples, 261 week blocks, seed 20260901), matching wave 1's construction exactly. DECISION (AGENTS.md EV rule, probability_positive>0.5 favors the candidate): wave 2 is the favourite over wave 1 at probability_positive 0.8235, so the served tiebreaker total SHOULD move to wave 2 -- proposed, not wired, this session (src/nfl_ats/tiebreaker.py is another agent's active file and off-limits to WP18). Proposed change on adoption: add a model_total_view_wave2 in src/nfl_ats/totals_wave2.py mirroring nfl_ats.totals.model_total_view but sourcing WAVE2_FEATURES/game_features_pbp.parquet, then repoint nfl_ats.tiebreaker's totals-view call at it; TOTALS_RESIDUAL_WEIGHT stays numerically 0.1 (wave 2's own chosen k) -- what changes is which fitted model produces the blended residual, not the blend weight itself.

weak_stack_v3_nfl_opener_confirmation.classification_evidence: PRIMARY (opener grade, production probability rule, n=1,537 paired games, 107 weeks, 2020-2025): baseline 53.36% vs candidate 53.03%, paired candidate-minus-baseline delta -0.333 pts, week-blocked 95% CI [-2.107, +1.467] pts, P+ 0.3415; season-blocked (6 season blocks -- below MIN_BLOCKS_FOR_INTERVAL=10, degenerate, reported for completeness only) delta -0.333 pts, CI [-1.596, +0.915] pts, P+ 0.2966. Both intervals cross zero, so per AGENTS.md's binding rule this stays unresolved_below_power (category 3), not refuted -- the naive week-blocked interval does not even sit entirely below zero, so no widening-factor check is needed to rule out wrong_sign_resolved. EV read at the opener (primary, pool-relevant grade): P+ 0.3415 for the candidate, i.e. roughly 2-to-1 the incumbent weak_stack is better here, not strong enough to promote and not strong enough to refute the gap features either.

SECONDARY (opener grade, historical sign rule residual_at_open>0, same paired games; per AGENTS.md may never veto the primary and did not need to): delta -0.732 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.211, season-blocked P+ 0.279 -- same direction, somewhat stronger lean against.
SECONDARY (close grade, same paired games; per AGENTS.md a close-graded number may never veto the opener-graded primary): probability rule delta +0.332 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.619, season-blocked P+ 0.586; sign rule delta +0.133 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.545. Direction flips vs the opener (mildly favours the candidate at close) -- the two grades disagree, exactly the situation AGENTS.md's opener-grading rule exists to adjudicate; the primary verdict above is the opener number.
CALIBRATION DIRECTION (Brier/log-loss, opener-graded paired games): both lean AGAINST the candidate -- Brier P+ 0.193 week / 0.246 season, log-loss P+ 0.181 week / 0.230 season. Consistent with the accuracy lean, not contradicting it.

weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.classification_evidence: The ENTIRE week-blocked interval [-3.3467, -0.5940] sits below zero, and the season-blocked interval [-3.2720, -0.8291] does too, with P+ 0.00255 and 0.0 respectively. That is a RESOLVED wrong sign on this endpoint -- the admissible closing ground wrong_sign_resolved -- not an interval-contains-zero rejection. Paired Brier and log-loss at the opener agree and also exclude zero (-0.001574 [-0.002839, -0.000336] P+ 0.0064; -0.003192 [-0.005787, -0.000648] P+ 0.0071), so the probability quality moved the same way as the picks. Scope of this closure is EXACTLY this construction: six continuous forecast columns added to a ~275-column ridge at alpha=10 under the sign rule. It closes nothing about forecast weather as a phenomenon -- see notes.
weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.description: Same run and same paired 1,537-game population as weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_probability_rule, scored under the predeclared SIGN rule (residual_at_open > 0) rather than the production probability rule. Baseline 52.83%, candidate 50.90%. Reported for comparability with prior opener-grade runs; the probability rule is the primary endpoint per docs/opener_evaluation.md.
weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.notes: Does NOT touch the registered pick-level forecast cells. forecast_weather_kn_warm_team_cold_late_full (+0.1686 accuracy points, week-blocked [+0.0091, +0.3169], P+ 0.9800) and its siblings are a different construction -- a narrow post-prediction pick-level tilt on ~1.5% of the slate -- and remain live as prospective challengers. This arm tested whether ridge extracts MORE from the raw continuous variables than those hand-coded cells do; it does not, on this population. Inferred mechanism, not measured: the market prices the same public forecast, so the columns mostly add variance to a market-residual model that is already near-sufficient, consistent with this project's own team-quality-is-already-priced finding. 142 picks flipped under the probability rule and the baseline was right on 55.8% of them versus the candidate's 44.2%, so the flips were actively harmful rather than neutral.

weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.classification_evidence: Recorded category 3 DESPITE being a control arm, because the strict AGENTS.md ground is 'bounded by a positive control PROVEN ABLE to detect an effect that size', and this run proves no such detection capability -- it shows an absence, which is not the same thing. The week-blocked interval [-2.8170, +0.4610] contains zero, so no wrong sign is resolved either. What IS measured, and what makes this decision-relevant: the oracle arm (-1.131 pts) and the real-forecast arm weak_stack_v4 (-1.065 pts) are statistically indistinguishable, so the ORACLE-MINUS-FORECAST GAP is -0.066 accuracy points. That gap is the entire headroom available to better weather forecasting on this path, and it is approximately zero and slightly negative. Reliability is not_applicable: this is a whole-profile comparison, not a per-team trait with a year-over-year value to split-half.
weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.description: POSITIVE-CONTROL arm: production weak_stack plus the weather that ACTUALLY happened (observed temp/wind, a forecast of infinite skill), vs the active weak_stack profile at the OPENER grade under the production probability rule. Deliberately leaky and never promotable; it exists to bound what ANY improvement in weather forecasting could be worth. Both arms hold ridge_alpha=10.0 and regressor=ridge fixed, on the same 1,537 paired Tuesday-opener games over 2020-2025, so the only difference from the weak_stack_v4 forecast arm is forecast skill. Baseline 53.3599%, oracle 52.2289%. Predeclared in docs/weak_stack_v4.md before scoring.
weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.notes: Answers the owner hypothesis that the forecast arm failed because forecasting is not accurate enough. Measured, that is not the explanation: the kickoff-nearest archive has a median 6.0-hour lead time and temperature r=0.964 / MAE 3.25F against the observed value, and this arm shows that even PERFECT weather does not help. Wind is the leg where the hypothesis had teeth (r=0.649, MAE 3.16 mph at that same lead), and the oracle covers wind too -- so a better wind source has a measured ceiling of about -0.07 points on this construction. Scope: this is the FEATURE-vector construction only. It says nothing about the pick-level weather CELLS, which are a different construction on ~1.5% of the slate and remain ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE challengers (forecast_weather_kn_warm_team_cold_late at P+ 0.9800, forecast_weather_kn_precip_high_total, forecast_cold_visitor_tilt). Coverage caveat: observed weather exists for 3,010 of 4,902 rows (61.4%) -- indoor games and unmapped stations have none -- so this is an oracle over the games that have an observation, with nulls imputed on the training fold like every other family.
weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.plain_summary: Oracle: model handed the weather that actually happened.

xlg05_transfer_cfb_prior.classification_evidence: Close-graded per the predeclaration's grade discipline: no terminal classification at this grade regardless of sign, and the sign here is POSITIVE anyway (+0.134 pts, tie-aware P+ 0.652 week-blocked, 0.860 season-blocked). refuted_mechanism unavailable on both grounds -- the week-blocked interval [-0.669,+0.926] straddles zero and its point estimate favours the candidate, and no_split_half_reliability was ruled out IN THE PREDECLARATION (section 6) because this family's arms differ in the ESTIMATOR, not in a feature column, so no trait exists to split. bounded_by_control unavailable: the positive control proved the harness detects a 49-accuracy-point effect, which bounds nothing at the fractions-of-a-point scale at issue.
xlg05_transfer_cfb_prior.description: XLG-05 arm (c), CFB-PRETRAINED: a generalized ridge whose PRIOR MEAN is theta_cfb, the CFB-only fit on the same feature space (fit on y - X*theta_cfb, then theta_cfb added back), versus arm (a) the NFL-only ridge that shrinks toward zero. Both on the IDENTICAL 14-column shared feature subset S at the frozen ridge_alpha=10.0 against market_residual -- nothing new derived or tuned. Tests a MODEL change (where the estimator shrinks its coefficients), NOT a team-quality feature. Close-graded, walk-forward weekly, min_train_games=50. Predeclared in docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md before any outcome number.
xlg05_transfer_cfb_prior.notes: Paired candidate-minus-baseline on 746 non-push games, 51 weeks, 3 seasons, rotation window [2011,2013] assigned by 'nfl-ats rotation assign'. Levels: cfb_prior 51.072% vs nfl_only 50.938%. Only 7 of 746 picks differ (4 better / 3 worse) -- the effect is small because at the frozen alpha=10 the prior moves home_cover_probability by at most 0.016 (about 0.55 points of predicted margin, measured on the 2011 slice), which flips a forced pick only within about half a point of the fence. Week-blocked 95% CI [-0.669,+0.926]; RECORDED probability_positive 0.6525 is TIE-AWARE, raw mean(draws>0) is 0.596 with a 0.113 tie share (docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md section 6a). Season-blocked 95% CI [0.000,+0.408], raw P+ 0.720 / tie-aware 0.860 (only 3 blocks; low combinatorial diversity, read as secondary). Observed delta sits at the 41.0th percentile of its own within-week permutation null (null mean +0.076 pts). Reliability field deliberately LEFT NULL: the analogue measured here is prior-vector stability -- theta_cfb fit on odd vs even CFB seasons is ANTI-correlated, r=-0.5333, cosine -0.4986 (1128/1183 pre-window 2006-2010 rows) -- which is NOT trait reliability and must not be read as a no_split_half_reliability closure. S contains three exact collinearities by construction (diff = home - away for the EPA triples), so that anti-correlation is more plausibly a design defect in S than a fact about football; removing the redundant diff_* columns is a cheap CFB-only follow-up. This measurement CONTRADICTS docs/scaling_and_transfer.md's written expectation that alpha=10 would bind harder on NFL's smaller per-window training sets than it did at Group-of-Five scale: at 512-1,264 NFL training rows the prior is if anything more inert on the pick. Correlated with xlg05_transfer_naive_pooled and xlg05_transfer_partial_pooled: same window, same baseline arm, one look.
xlg05_transfer_cfb_prior.plain_summary: Instead of starting the NFL model from nothing, we started it from what 12,500 college games say the same inputs are worth. It changed 7 picks out of 746 and got 4 of them right -- a very small lean in the transfer's favour, on far too few changed picks to act on.

xlg05_transfer_naive_pooled.notes: Paired candidate-minus-baseline on 746 non-push games (765 scored), 51 weeks, 3 seasons, rotation window [2011,2013] assigned by 'nfl-ats rotation assign' (family xlg05_transfer_prior, close, no inheritance, no --acknowledge-mined). Levels: naive_pooled 50.938% vs nfl_only 50.938%, exact tie. 220 of 746 picks differ, split 110 better / 110 worse. Week-blocked 95% CI [-2.957,+3.200]; the RECORDED probability_positive 0.5225 is TIE-AWARE (P(better)+0.5*P(tie)); the raw mean(draws>0) is 0.509 with a 0.027 tie share (see docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md section 6a, an amendment disclosed between the null check and the screen: mean(draws>0) scores a dead heat as a certain loss). Season-blocked 95% CI [-1.600,+1.195], raw P+ 0.422 / tie-aware 0.532. This arm picks home 55.6% vs the baseline's 51.8%, so its within-week permutation null is centred at -1.219 pts, not zero; the observed +0.000 sits at the 74.5th percentile of that null. Reliability field deliberately LEFT NULL: the honest analogue measured here is prior-vector stability (theta_cfb odd vs even CFB seasons, r=-0.5333, cosine -0.4986, 1128/1183 pre-window rows), which is NOT trait reliability and must not be read as a no_split_half_reliability closure -- recording it in that field would invite exactly that error. Correlated with xlg05_transfer_cfb_prior and xlg05_transfer_partial_pooled: same window, same baseline arm, three views of one look, not three independent votes.
xlg05_transfer_naive_pooled.plain_summary: We trained one model on NFL and college games together instead of NFL games alone. It changed 220 of 746 picks and got exactly 110 of them right and 110 wrong -- a dead-even coin flip. No change to what we play.

xlg05_transfer_partial_pooled.classification_evidence: Close-graded per the predeclaration's grade discipline: no terminal classification at this grade regardless of sign. This arm is an EXACT TIE with the baseline -- 0 of 746 picks differ -- so refuted_mechanism is unavailable for want of any sign at all, let alone a resolved wrong one; the recorded probability_positive 0.500 is the tie-aware value (P(better)+0.5*P(tie)), and the raw mean(draws>0) of 0.000 is an artifact of scoring a dead heat as a loss, not evidence against the candidate (docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md section 6a). no_split_half_reliability was ruled out IN THE PREDECLARATION (section 6): the arms differ in the ESTIMATOR, not in a feature column, so no trait exists to split. bounded_by_control unavailable: the positive control proved the harness detects a 49-accuracy-point effect, which bounds nothing at this scale.
xlg05_transfer_partial_pooled.description: XLG-05 arm (d), PARTIALLY POOLED: generalized ridge toward kappa*theta_cfb, with the prior STRENGTH kappa chosen by leave-one-season-out on TRAINING seasons only over the frozen grid {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}; kappa=0 reproduces arm (a) exactly and kappa=1 reproduces arm (c) exactly, so the arm is an interpolation containing both neighbours rather than a third mechanism. Versus arm (a), the NFL-only ridge. Both on the IDENTICAL 14-column shared feature subset S at the frozen ridge_alpha=10.0 against market_residual -- only kappa is selected, the alpha is never tuned. Tests a MODEL change, NOT a team-quality feature. Close-graded, walk-forward weekly, min_train_games=50. Predeclared in docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md before any outcome number.
xlg05_transfer_partial_pooled.notes: Paired candidate-minus-baseline on 746 non-push games, 51 weeks, 3 seasons, rotation window [2011,2013] assigned by 'nfl-ats rotation assign'. EXACT TIE: 0 of 746 picks differ, both arms 50.938%, week- and season-blocked CIs are point masses at [0,0]. The selection was genuinely exercised, not pinned: kappa = 0.00 in 34 weeks, 0.25 in 1, 0.50 in 1, 0.75 in 1, 1.00 in 14, with ZERO LOSO fallbacks (every week had 2-5 usable training seasons). The prior does move the coefficients -- theta_d - theta_a is non-zero in 17 of 51 weeks -- but at the frozen alpha=10 it shifts home_cover_probability by at most 0.016 (~0.55 points of predicted margin), too little to cross the 0.5 forced-pick threshold on any game here. TEAM-QUALITY BOUND CHECK (owner's 'team quality is already priced'): the bound cannot apply by construction since all arms share one design, and the decomposition sharpens that -- 96.2% of the prior's squared coefficient movement lands in the six team-quality (EPA) columns, while the prior_market_only diagnostic arm, which forbids the prior from touching any of them, ALSO changes zero picks. Zero gain on both sides of the partition, so there is no gain to attribute to team quality and none outside it. That diagnostic arm is deliberately NOT recorded as its own signal: it is a correlated decomposition of this same window. Reliability field deliberately LEFT NULL -- see xlg05_transfer_cfb_prior's notes for the prior-vector stability measurement (r=-0.5333) and why it must not be read as trait reliability. Correlated with the other two xlg05_transfer_* entries: same window, same baseline arm, one look.
xlg05_transfer_partial_pooled.plain_summary: We let the model decide for itself, season by season, how much to trust the college-football starting point. On this window it ended up playing exactly the same 746 picks as the NFL-only model -- an identical card, so there is nothing here to act on either way.

xlg06_rookie_prior_stage1_rb.notes: WP46 dedicated follow-up on the secondary RB read flagged in the QB write-up (xlg06_rookie_prior_stage1_qb's notes field). Population/predictor/outcome/statistic/reliability method identical to the QB cell, position swapped to RB, via scripts/xlg06_rb_stage1.py which imports scripts/xlg06_rookie_prior_cfb_screen.py's functions UNCHANGED. --mode screen reused the original script's own RB seeds (cohort 4000, player 4100, reliability cohort 1001, player 1101) and reproduced its already-computed RB numbers exactly (r=0.06443485228551912 to 1e-6, matched by tests/test_xlg06_rb_stage1.py). Player-blocked secondary coherence check: r=0.06443 (same point estimate), CI [+0.00438,+0.12327], P+ 0.98175 -- agrees with the cohort-blocked primary. Per-cohort trend (13 individual cohort years, player-blocked within-cohort, descriptive only): 12 of 13 cohorts read positive point estimates (only 2013 negative, r=-0.090), only 2022's own CI sits entirely positive [+0.0457,+0.3660] and every other single cohort's own CI crosses zero -- MORE consistent across cohorts than the QB cell's per-cohort trend (which ranged -0.215 to +0.259 with no consistent sign). Positive-control (leaked monotone rank-transform of rating as the outcome) drove Pearson r to 0.9690 (cohort) / 0.9690 (player) and Spearman rho to 1.0/1.0, P+ 1.0 both blockings -- confirms the bootstrap machinery correctly reports a strong effect when one is engineered, but this is a code-path sanity check only, not sized to the real ~0.06 effect, so it is never cited as this cell's closing ground. This is Stage-1 CFB-only evidence about whether an RB usage prior is worth building at Stage 2 (crosswalk + NFL join, unbuilt); it is not an NFL claim.
xlg06_rookie_prior_stage1_rb.plain_summary: Does a recruit's star rating predict how much a true freshman RUNNING BACK actually plays in college?
